docs.title: Prequel (1945 - 2026)
docs.text: Takes place between 1945 - 2026. This era tells the story of how Ingram, founder of the Cobalt Intervention Corps (CIC), discovers the Kindred prophecy and begins his ruthless quest to steal divinity for himself, setting the stage for the Genesis event.

docs.title: 1 The Alps Contract
docs.text:
• Act 1: Introduce Ingram (18) and Dante (16) working in tandem on a rescue mission in the Alps to save the children of the Order's leadership.
  • Act 2: The tense rescue of the stranded party from a hazardous environment.
  • Act 3: Ingram observes that a large number of the Order members have deviated from the primary mission for a secret objective.

docs.title: 2 The Cache of Scrolls
docs.text:
• Act 1: Ingram discovers the Order members have gone to a hidden cave sealed with an unknown script.
  • Act 2: He eavesdrops as they unearth a cache of prophetic scrolls and ancient relics.
  • Act 3: After the Order departs, Ingram waits them out, then steals a few scrolls and expensive-looking relics for himself.

docs.title: 3 The Translation
docs.text:
• Act 1: Ingram and the Order independently begin translating their found relics.
  • Act 2: The Order and Dante discover the full Kindred Pact and the truth it explains about the bloodlines and the purpose of their genealogy.
  • Act 3: Ingram discovers the history of the Vessel lineage and the power they possess, learning that the mantle of divinity can be shifted if a line is ended. His path is set.

docs.title: 4 The False Sinkhole
docs.text:
• Act 1: Using information from the scrolls, Ingram starts plotting. The Order begins tracking potential Vessels outside their maintained bloodlines.
  • Act 2: Ingram engineers a disaster to uncover a large trove of Order relics, capitalizing on it with monetary gains and a "convenient" and immediate CIC response.
  • Act 3: Ingram lays low, using his new information and resources to advance his plans for CIC's genetic research branches.

docs.title: 5 An Explosion of Wealth
docs.text:
• Act 1: The financial gains from Ingram's ventures propel his company into a period of exponential growth.
  • Act 2: CIC becomes a household name like the Red Cross, granting Ingram global access and influence.
  • Act 3: CIC begins aggressively buying up startups and labs specializing in groundbreaking genetic and genealogical research.

docs.title: 6 The Disappearances
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Order starts noticing that a large number of the people they have been tracking have started either dying or disappearing under mysterious circumstances.
  • Act 2: Dante pieces together the clues and realizes the horrifying truth of what Ingram is doing.
  • Act 3: It becomes a desperate race to identify and secure the remaining Vessels before Ingram can get to them.

docs.title: 7 The Man Who Knows
docs.text:
• Act 1: By a chance of luck, the Order's path crosses with a US military operative named David in Europe.
  • Act 2: They immediately realize something is different about him and how he seems to know too much about their secret organization. They make an effort to get a DNA sample.
  • Act 3: They discover he is an anomaly of the highest degree: he has all 100 genetic markers of the Vessels.

docs.title: 8 The Last Heir
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Order secures David by faking his death, and he is reported KIA to his loved ones.
  • Act 2: David tips them off that Ingram is up to something serious and that the Blue Line of Vessels is in immediate danger.
  • Act 3: The Order prepares a desperate, last-ditch attack on Ingram's Montana Stronghold.

docs.title: 9 Misplaced Power
docs.text:
• Act 1: The fight is fast but loud as the Order infiltrates and attempts to secure the facility.
  • Act 2: Ingram, cornered, reveals his final tragic piece: an orphan he adopted and raised, the last of the Blue Family Line.
  • Act 3: Her execution by firearm triggers the event. The transfer of divinity bypasses Ingram and flows to Dante, the next stable line in the vicinity, robbing Ingram of his victory.

docs.title: Age of Genesis (2026 - 2028)
docs.text:
Takes place starting at midnight in the spring of 2026. A large EMP knocks out every electronic on the planet. Over the next week, hyper-accelerated flora growth releases a fatal pollen, wiping out 75% of the world's population and forcing survivors to high ground.

East Coast

docs.title: Survive
docs.text: The players must start in their hometown, deal with the initial fallout, and try to survive, ultimately leading to their awakening.

docs.title: 10 The Blackout
docs.text:
• Act 1: The first barrier: players are locked in their location by a nonfunctional electronic door.
  • Act 2: Info gathering, potential people interactions, and the panic of the silent apocalypse starts setting in.
  • Act 3: The players must avoid a mob of angry and confused people. It's clear they need to get out of the population center.

docs.title: 11 The Choice
docs.text:
• Act 1: The air is becoming strange, thicker, and harder to breathe. The only solution is to head east to higher ground.
  • Act 2: They encounter Lt. Mason from the CIC Washington County Reserve Unit and his squad, equipped with analog gear, rations, and transportation.
  • Act 3: The choice of authoritarian safety with them or dangerous freedom on their own is posed.

docs.title: 12 The Tollmen and Shade
docs.text:
• Act 1: Introduce Slash and Hooker as the mechanics the crew finds on their travels.
  • Act 2: A run-in with a group of thugs (The Tollmen) harassing a youth, Shade, and attempting to set a barn he’s hiding in on fire.
  • Act 3: The Awakening: Shade literally vanishes, and this catalyst causes the players to use their first Keywords.

docs.title: Build
docs.text: The players have established a base of operations and now start dealing with the immediate issues of their region.

docs.title: 13 Shade’s Request
docs.text:
• Act 1: The players have established a safe and secure place away from the pollen fog.
  • Act 2: Shade suddenly appears in the player’s camp, wounded and pleading for help for his friends detained by the CIC.
  • Act 3: The players crash the CIC safehouse interrogation and rescue Riannon, Willie, and Izzy.

docs.title: 14 The Chimera Facility and Angela
docs.text:
• Act 1: The group discovers an anomaly around a small building where the closer you approach, the further it appears to be away. They are approached by a young adult named Lillith.
  • Act 2: Lillith (a former Chimera employee) explains the spatial anomaly was her doing to contain a beast. She asks for help putting it down for good.
  • Act 3: Back at the settlement, a large exodus of strangers from the north has arrived, led by a natural leader named Angela.

docs.title: 15 The Radiants and Lt. Mason
docs.text:
• Act 1: The community grows into a stronghold of skilled survivors with the arrival of Angela's group.
  • Act 2: A CIC camp is discovered nearby. It is Lt. Mason, who has deserted CIC and is now working for his own survival.
  • Act 3: A mysterious signal in the sky leads to a college, where a CIC squad led by a Red Aura user has abducted an e-sports team. The Red Aura leader flees, and the players rescue the team.

docs.title: Secure
docs.text: A clear and immediate threat is identified, and the East Coast needs to be secured from CIC, Chimera, and a new zombie-like "ROT" from Florida.

docs.title: 16 Tennessee Chimera Facility
docs.text:
• Act 1: Survivors arrive speaking of anomalies in Tennessee, prompting an investigation.
  • Act 2: The group finds a Chimera facility guarded by mutated humanoid beasts.
  • Act 3: Infiltrating the facility leads to the discovery of "soul cages" and a fight with the heads of Chimera.

docs.title: 17 Ohio CIC Warlord
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Kindred in hiding reveal themselves and explain the threat of Ingram and CIC.
  • Act 2: The Red Aura CIC leader who escaped has grown stronger and has become a militaristic warlord in Ohio.
  • Act 3: A large-scale fight leads to the Ohio facility being destroyed and becoming a new stronghold for the players' community.

docs.title: 18 Florida Orphanage
docs.text:
• Act 1: A strange, non-corporeal girl named Whisper arrives in the settlement and delivers a warning.
  • Act 2: Refugees report attacks made by "feral" humans in the south.
  • Act 3: The group travels to Florida, finds the orphanage, and learns it was a Chimera/CIC facility where Whisper and her brother ("The Rot") were forced to awaken. The Rot is destroyed, bringing him peace.

docs.title: Zion
docs.text: Heading westward to discover a religious settlement in Kansas, where issues cause Dante to ask the players to seek help in Vegas.

docs.title: 19 Quincy and George
docs.text:
• Act 1: The players receive word that there is a friendly settlement west along the Mississippi.
  • Act 2: They discover Rivertown, run by Quincy, a refugee from a religious fortress called New Zion.
  • Act 3: A giant mutated cow, George, protects the town, but other local cows have become cannibalistic and must be dealt with.

docs.title: 20 New Zion and Dante
docs.text:
• Act 1: After helping Quincy, the group decides to find the religious fortress of New Zion in Kansas.
  • Act 2: New Zion is a dogmatic faction run by Joseph, a Vessel candidate currently being watched by Dante.
  • Act 3: Dante requests the players go to Vegas and find a woman named Skye, who can help the people of Zion.

docs.title: 21 Road to Vegas / The Twins
docs.text:
• Act 1: The group travels across the plains and eventually to a canyon.
  • Act 2: The canyon is a trap set by mercenaries hired to steal resources from travelers.
  • Act 3: After surviving the ambush, the group is attacked by twinned Awakened who use powerful manipulation of earth and metals.

docs.title: Vegas
docs.text: Vegas is an apocalyptic town of indulgence, ruled by the charismatic Skye. CIC raids the city to kidnap Skye's lover for her genetic uniqueness.

docs.title: 22 Skye’s Games
docs.text:
• Act 1: Vegas is a lawless town held together by the martial rule of Skye, a former performer.
  • Act 2: To gain an audience with Skye, the group must prove their worth in her gladiatorial games.
  • Act 3: The final round of fights pits the group against Skye’s second in command.

docs.title: 23 CIC Raid
docs.text:
• Act 1: The fight is interrupted by a CIC squad dropping into the arena, setting off explosions and attacking the crowd.
  • Act 2: The fight is over quickly, and Skye is impressed, but realizes the attack was a diversion.
  • Act 3: The group has their audience with Skye and proposes an alliance between Zion and Vegas.

docs.title: 24 Negotiations
docs.text:
• Act 1: The negotiations go smoothly, and an agreement for trade and safe passage is reached.
  • Act 2: The negotiations are interrupted by news that Skye’s lover, Sarah, has been kidnapped by CIC.
  • Act 3: A jaded victory now leads to a decision: return to Zion or find Sarah.

docs.title: Montana
docs.text: The group discovers the purist community of Sanctuary, which must be dealt with to reveal the location of a mountain facility where Ingram holds a final, terrible ultimatum.

docs.title: 25 Sanctuary
docs.text:
• Act 1: The search for Sarah leads the group north. Whisper appears and points them toward Silas in Montana.
  • Act 2: The path leads them to the town of Sanctuary, a "purist" society where no Awakened are allowed.
  • Act 3: The group discovers the town leader, Joe, is secretly Awakened and pressure him to reveal the entrance to the CIC facility.

docs.title: 26 Silas
docs.text:
• Act 1: The facility is deep in the mountain, full of abandoned offices and a mysterious scent.
  • Act 2: The lower floors are a horror scene, leading to a lab at the bottom.
  • Act 3: A man named Silas taunts the group, revealing Chimera’s culmination: soul cages and a device to artificially create Vessels. The players see dossiers on all of the Kindred.

docs.title: 27 The Pact and The Ultimatum
docs.text:
• Act 1: The group confronts the Kindred, who give them the whole story (the Pact, the prequel, the Order, and David).
  • Act 2: The meeting is interrupted by a messenger: CIC has captured Tim, Patrick's friend and the last of the Silver Line of Vessels.
  • Act 3: War is declared. The players now realize they have to take the fight to California.

docs.title: The State of California
docs.text: The players make it to California to a sterile, militaristic fascist utopia where the Awakened are a higher class of citizen.

docs.title: 28 The Rockies
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Rockies are dangerous grounds, with treacherous travel and large avian beasts ruling the sky.
  • Act 2: The landscape is unforgiving, with a singular extended family being the only rest stop.
  • Act 3: The other side of the range is scorched earth, a buffer zone where war was waged on nature itself.

docs.title: 29 Ingram's Utopia
docs.text:
• Act 1: California is filled with sterile, uniform, soulless micro-communities.
  • Act 2: The security system is based on genetic readers; your DNA is your only value.
  • Act 3: The players discover that this community has chosen this fascism and are the problem.

docs.title: 30 The First Stone is Cast
docs.text:
• Act 1: The group is discovered, and the community they are in goes into a lockdown.
  • Act 2: The security deployment is made up of "blanks" in super-powered psionic equipment, treated like slaves.
  • Act 3: The Proctor of the community is an Orange Aura user, battle-tested and smart, whose militia goes toe-to-toe with the players.

docs.title: The City of San Francisco
docs.text: Whisper tips the players off to a weakness in Ingram's fortress and the location of Tim, leading to an all-out war.

docs.title: 31 Whispers of Urgency
docs.text:
• Act 1: With the first contact being violent, war is assured. Whisper provides a glimmer of hope: a crack in Ingram's defenses.
  • Act 2: The plan is put together: a diversionary war to allow the players to get to Ingram and Tim.
  • Act 3: Resistance from allies is assuaged by the reality that Ingram will not stop at California.

docs.title: 32 War of Genesis
docs.text:
• Act 1: The first wave is to get the attention of Ingram's Forces, pulling the fight away from civilians.
  • Act 2: The second wave is a war of attrition as both sides fight for their survival.
  • Act 3: At the height of the conflict, the players make their move, only to find Silas in their way.

docs.title: 33 Breaching the Barrier
docs.text:
• Act 1: Silas has returned, stronger and smarter, now able to make blood clones of himself.
  • Act 2: The fight with Silas is a small war of its own.
  • Act 3: With her story put to rest, Whisper generates a new body for herself. The energy released shatters the barrier.

docs.title: Alcatraz
docs.text: A psychological test of self, leading to a final confrontation with a mutated and superpowered Ingram.

docs.title: 34 The Mind Prison
docs.text:
• Act 1: Alcatraz sits silently, the bay vacant of security.
  • Act 2: The prison's defense is a psychic illusion blanketing the facility, pitting one's own thoughts against them.
  • Act 3: The group navigates the illusion and confronts the "Mirror," silencing Ingram's last elite guard.

docs.title: 35 The Confrontation
docs.text:
• Act 1: Ingram is not immediately hostile; he is calm and speaks as if doing them a favor.
  • Act 2: Tim is alive, but restrained in a device similar to the one that held the corpse of Sarah.
  • Act 3: Ingram activates an object on his chest and is immediately altered into a peak physical being as Tim is rendered unconscious.

docs.title: 36 A World Reborn
docs.text:
• Act 1: Ingram boasts and once again attempts to convert the group to join him in a final offer of mercy.
  • Act 2: The group chooses to engage. An epic fight ensues, leaving Alcatraz a pile of rubble and ending Ingram's Reign.
  • Act 3: A year has passed. Humanity has migrated to Dubai to build Metropolis over the Orange Wellspring. The Kindred return to the Weave, and the heroes are given their final choice.

docs.title: Age of Exploitation (100 Years After Alcatraz)
docs.text: A cyberpunk city has risen in Dubai, but a divide has grown between the Awakened and non-awakened. The age begins when the Orange Nexus is corrupted by the city's overconsumption.

docs.title: 37 The First Gig
docs.text:
• Act 1: The phone call for a simple job.
  • Act 2: The client is late, tension rises.
  • Act 3: The job goes wrong when a power surge hits the city.

docs.title: 38 The Surge
docs.text:
• Act 1: A city-wide blackout.
  • Act 2: A masked figure interrupts the deal.
  • Act 3: The players escape with only a briefcase.

docs.title: 39 011.E (Ollie)
docs.text:
• Act 1: A voice comes from inside the case.
  • Act 2: The players hack open the box.
  • Act 3: It's a unique bot, who has the power to Awaken others.

docs.title: 40 The Callback
docs.text:
• Act 1: The client demands a redo.
  • Act 2: The players must arrange the new handoff themselves to pay for their mistake.
  • Act 3: They set up the meeting.

docs.title: 41 The Exchange
docs.text:
• Act 1: The exchange is tense and dangerous.
  • Act 2: The target is a small case with glass cubes inside.
  • Act 3: The deal is completed successfully.

docs.title: 42 The Eidetic Drive
docs.text:
• Act 1: The bot, Ollie, knows what the cubes are.
  • Act 2: They are Eidetic Drives, a lost technology from the fall of Alcatraz.
  • Act 3: Ollie begins analyzing them.

docs.title: 43 Big Opportunity
docs.text:
• Act 1: The group gets an offer for off-the-books security for a corporation.
  • Act 2: The job is to guard an experimental Nexus tapping project in Moscow.
  • Act 3: The fine print: they need to acquire their own license and gear.

docs.title: 44 License Acquisition
docs.text:
• Act 1: They need to steal or forge a contractor's license.
  • Act 2: They need to buy, or "creatively acquire," high-end gear.
  • Act 3: They successfully prepare for the mission.

docs.title: 45 The Moscow Incident
docs.text:
• Act 1: The group arrives in Moscow.
  • Act 2: All their prep is rendered moot when the Nexus explodes with energy.
  • Act 3: The explosion spawns alien beasts and warps the environment, creating the first God Beast.

docs.title: 46 Off the Hook
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Moscow Incident starts two major shifts: a corporate race to tap Nexuses.
  • Act 2: And monster hunting goes from an occupation to a televised sport.
  • Act 3: The party becomes legendary for surviving Moscow and becomes in-demand Hunters.

docs.title: 47 Toronto and The Hive
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Green Nexus in Toronto falls, creating a chaotic jungle.
  • Act 2: The area is overrun by an insectoid race known as The Hive.
  • Act 3: The players are hired for a high-risk VIP rescue inside the anomaly.

docs.title: 48 West Virginia, Humanity’s Archive
docs.text:
• Act 1: The players investigate the Null Wellspring in West Virginia.
  • Act 2: They discover The Archive, a living repository of human history.
  • Act 3: Ollie connects to the Archive, allowing him to begin decrypting the Eidetic Drives.

docs.title: 49 Alcatraz Memorial, Legends Never Die
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Blue Nexus in the ruins of San Francisco falls.
  • Act 2: The area becomes a treacherous underwater zone haunted by a Prehistoric Penguin God Beast.
  • Act 3: A corporation hires the crew for a discrete data-retrieval mission in the submerged ruins.

docs.title: 50 Utah, The Anchor is Shifted
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Purple Nexus in Salt Lake collapses.
  • Act 2: The area is now the domain of a Great Frog God Beast, hoarding all it can find.
  • Act 3: A mysterious client hires the crew to steal a specific server vault from the beast's hoard.

docs.title: 51 Taiwan’s Inevitability
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Red Nexus in Taiwan falls, becoming a volcanic hellscape.
  • Act 2: The zone is ruled by a Three-Headed Dog God Beast of pure rage.
  • Act 3: A corporation hires the crew for a "field test" contract to eliminate a lesser beast for a live broadcast.

docs.title: 52 The Exodus of The Order
docs.text:
• Act 1: A mysterious, catastrophic energy event rocks Metropolis.
  • Act 2: A massive, unidentified object launches from a hidden silo into space.
  • Act 3: Ollie confirms it coincided with a massive data dump from the Orange Nexus, but the connection is a mystery.

docs.title: 53 The Black Harvest
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Black Nexus falls, becoming a place of fear and decay.
  • Act 2: A cunning Rat God Beast, the Nezumi, now rules the area.
  • Act 3: A corporation hires the crew for a "hostile asset acquisition" under the guise of a routine cleanup.

docs.title: 54 Judgement Down Under
docs.text:
• Act 1: The White Nexus falls. A corporation hires the crew for "specimen extraction."
  • Act 2: They find the newly-formed God Beast: a terrifying Sphinx who judges all she sees.
  • Act 3: She deems the crew "tainted, but not yet corrupted" and gives Ollie the final key to deciphering the prophecy, revealing the Order has fled Earth.

docs.title: 55 Lock and Key
docs.text:
• Act 1: After learning the truth from Ollie, the crew abandons their life as Hunters.
  • Act 2: Their new and final mission: stop the corporate coalition from tapping the final Silver Nexus in London.
  • Act 3: They must find a way past the True Dragon that guards it.

docs.title: 56 Infiltrating Eden
docs.text:
• Act 1: The crew launches a series of targeted strikes against the coalition's supply lines.
  • Act 2: They successfully delay the London operation, buying precious time.
  • Act 3: They gather intelligence on the coalition's ultimate weapon: a massive Nexus Drill.

docs.title: 57 Blueprints of The Apocalypse
docs.text:
• Act 1: The journey to London takes them through a blighted Ireland, mutated by the Dragon's presence.
  • Act 2: They infiltrate a corporate outpost to steal the final blueprints for the drill.
  • Act 3: They now have the information they need to stop the corporations' plan.

docs.title: 58 Race to London
docs.text:
• Act 1: The crew arrives to find London a massive warzone.
  • Act 2: The corporate coalition is laying siege to the city, battling the Dragon's brood.
  • Act 3: The players must navigate the three-way battlefield to reach the city center.

docs.title: 59 The Blockade
docs.text:
• Act 1: The players must fight their way through the corporate military blockade.
  • Act 2: They face elite soldiers and advanced war machines.
  • Act 3: They successfully breach the outer perimeter and enter the Dragon's territory.

docs.title: 60 The Nest
docs.text:
• Act 1: They enter the ruins of London, now the Dragon's nest.
  • Act 2: They fight their way through hundreds of newly hatched, desperate dragon offspring.
  • Act 3: They reach the inner sanctum where the True Dragon resides.

docs.title: 61 The First Dragon
docs.text:
• Act 1: The crew confronts the ancient True Dragon.
  • Act 2: The confrontation is a battle of wits and will, not just brute force.
  • Act 3: They narrowly win by exploiting a logical loophole in the Dragon's ancient duty.

docs.title: 62 Humanity
docs.text:
• Act 1: The players reach the colossal Nexus Drill and its final defense.
  • Act 2: A corporate All-Star team of elite security forces stands in their way.
  • Act 3: As they fight, the drill hits full power, torturing the Silver Kindred and washing the battlefield in psychic agony.

docs.title: 63 The Fall
docs.text:
• Act 1: The players fight to the core and trigger an overload, a moment of false victory.
  • Act 2: The drill's explosion destabilizes reality. The Silver Kindred, Chaos, enacts The Fall as a mercy killing for the world, a violent collapse where the very continents are unmade and reshaped into a new Pangea.
  • Act 3: Ollie, realizing there is no escape, sacrifices his consciousness to transfer the crew into the Archive as the world ends.

docs.title: Age of Atonement (500 Years After The Fall)
docs.text: Five hundred years after The Fall reshaped the world's continents into a new Pangea, the world has been repopulated by new races created by the lonely Kindred, Chaos. But the land is terrorized by the corrupted God Beasts.

docs.title: 64 New Awakenings
docs.text:
• Act 1: Five hundred years after The Fall, the God Beasts roam the new land as cruel tyrants.
  • Act 2: The new races struggle to survive. A group of humans, the first in centuries to have an aura, are born.
  • Act 3: These First Heroes and the leaders of the new races form The Guild to stop the beasts.

docs.title: 65 A Fighting Chance
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Guild sets its first mission: aiding the Catfolk and Bovine races.
  • Act 2: They devise a plan to trap the perpetually moving Yellow God Beast (The Bison).
  • Act 3: They succeed, trapping the beast in a moment of absolute stillness.

docs.title: 66 The Guild
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Guild's reputation grows. They are called upon by the Terra and Tortoise races.
  • Act 2: They devise a strategy to imprison the immense Green God Beast (The Tortoise).
  • Act 3: They trap the beast beneath a sea of desert sand, a patient prison for a patient creature.

docs.title: 67 The Unseen Chains
docs.text:
• Act 1: The next target is the Black God Beast (The Nezumi).
  • Act 2: The mission requires navigating the politics of the Ratfolk and Necros races.
  • Act 3: They successfully lock the beast beneath the ruins of a Second Age city.

docs.title: 68 The Raging Heart
docs.text:
• Act 1: The heroes travel to the volcanic isles to aid the Red Panda race.
  • Act 2: They must trap the Red God Beast (The Three-Headed Dog) within a volcano.
  • Act 3: It takes a great act of sacrifice, but they seal the beast within a super-alloy sphere.

docs.title: 69 The Perfect Cell
docs.text:
• Act 1: Trapping the White God Beast (The Sphinx) is a battle of wits, not strength.
  • Act 2: The heroes must convince the proud and judgmental beast to imprison itself.
  • Act 3: They succeed by having the Sphinx bind herself with her own vow of solitude.

docs.title: 70 The Mythic Foundation
docs.text:
• Act 1: The great Blue God Beast (The Penguin) is trapped in an undersea labyrinth.
  • Act 2: The prison is a series of puzzles that no one person could ever solve alone.
  • Act 3: The heroes and their allies work in perfect concert to seal the beast away.

docs.title: 71 A World at Peace
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Orange God Beast (The Trashfather) is trapped in a Rubik's Cube puzzle box from before the Renrock.
  • Act 2: The Purple God Beast (The Frog) is trapped in the vault of its own hoard, sealed by its own greed.
  • Act 3: With the final beasts imprisoned, the work is done. The First Heroes' mission is complete.

docs.title: 72 An Age of Peace
docs.text:
• Act 1: The First Heroes retire, ushering in generations of adventurers and exploration.
  • Act 2: Humanity once again loses its ability to gain aura, its purpose having been served.
  • Act 3: A golden age of relative peace and prosperity begins, lasting for several centuries.

docs.title: 73 The Library and the Curator
docs.text:
• Act 1: The golden age is dying. The prisons are psychically failing, leaking "sins" and corrupting the new races.
  • Act 2: The heroes of the Second Age, The Returned, are awakened from The Archive by The Curator.
  • Act 3: They learn their new purpose: to mend the minds of the Kindred and the hearts of the world's people.

docs.title: 74 Purple
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Returned's first mission: travel to the lands of the Aelph and Frogfolk.
  • Act 2: The Aelph's healthy mercantilism has become rapacious Greed, threatening their sacred forests.
  • Act 3: The heroes must help the Aelph find a path back to balance with their spiritual brethren.

docs.title: 75 Blue
docs.text:
• Act 1: The heroes travel to the northern tundra, home of the Bearfolk and Pengu.
  • Act 2: The Pengu's efficient collectivism has become insidious Manipulation, as they use economic warfare to assimilate other clans.
  • Act 3: The heroes must act as diplomats to save the independence of the Bearfolk.

docs.title: 76 Red
docs.text:
• Act 1: The heroes journey to the volcanic Eastern Isles of the Pyronim.
  • Act 2: The Mongrels' drive for strength has turned to honorless, explosive Rage, leading to a brutal war against the Red Panda.
  • Act 3: The heroes must find a way to quell the war and restore the balance of honorable rivalry.

docs.title: 77 White
docs.text:
• Act 1: The heroes journey to the lands of the Sphinx, now home to a new race.
  • Act 2: The people have been poisoned by the sin of Pride, leading to a rigid caste system.
  • Act 3: The heroes must teach them that all are worthy of compassion, not just the "pure."

docs.title: 78 Orange
docs.text:
• Act 1: The heroes travel to the ruins of Metropolis, now home to the Gnomes.
  • Act 2: The Gnomes' creativity has been twisted into Innovation without Purpose, creating dangerous and pointless contraptions.
  • Act 3: The heroes must show them that true invention comes from solving problems, not just creating them.

docs.title: 79 Black
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Returned act as diplomats to mend a schism in Necros society.
  • Act 2: The Necros' logical pragmatism has devolved into soul-crushing Tyranny under the influence of the Black prison's Fear.
  • Act 3: The heroes must restore a sense of justice and mercy to their leadership.

docs.title: 80 Green and Yellow
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Returned journey to the Tortoise nation, a culture so poisoned by Xenophobia from the Green prison they have walled themselves off.
  • Act 2: They then travel to the great plains, where the Bovine's healthy appetite has become mindless Gluttony due to the leaking sin of the Yellow prison.
  • Act 3: A montage shows the Guild's successes across the globe, mending cultural wounds and slowly restoring balance.

docs.title: 81 Silver
docs.text:
• Act 1: The work of mending the world nears completion.
  • Act 2: The heroes receive a secret, cosmic plea from the only uncorrupted Kindred: Chaos.
  • Act 3: Chaos has been wandering the planet, lonely and remorseful for centuries, and now reveals the heroes' final mission.

docs.title: 82 Immortality
docs.text:
• Act 1: A new group, The Final Heroes, are chosen by The Curator and bonded to The Archive, granting them a form of immortality.
  • Act 2: Following Chaos's guidance, they return to the prison of the Yellow God Beast.
  • Act 3: They must solve the puzzle of its sin by simply moving it out of its locked stasis, restoring responsible freedom.

docs.title: 83 The Puzzle in a Volcano
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Red Kindred needs her rage soothed. This requires a special quenching potion.
  • Act 2: Only the Mongrels know the recipe, and the heroes must earn their trust to acquire it.
  • Act 3: The superheated alloy sphere is quenched, and the Red Kindred is freed from her prison of rage.

docs.title: 84 The Vault Below the Arena
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Purple Kindred is imprisoned by her own hoard.
  • Act 2: To free her, the world-changing wealth she has gathered must be destroyed and purged.
  • Act 3: The heroes prove they are free of the temptation that ensnared her, and she is released.

docs.title: 85 The Ocean Prison
docs.text:
• Act 1: The last Kindred, Dante, is sealed in an underwater labyrinth.
  • Act 2: The complex requires immense teamwork to traverse and cannot be solved alone.
  • Act 3: The heroes use all the skills they have learned to navigate the prison and free the Blue Kindred.

docs.title: 86 The Ever-Moving Desert
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Green Kindred is freed when the stone foundation her statue rests on is destroyed.
  • Act 2: This act of "destruction" breaks down her hardened walls of self-imprisonment.
  • Act 3: She is released, learning that true security comes from being open to the world.

docs.title: 87 The Frozen Storm
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Black Kindred requires the heroes to traverse a treacherous and harrowing path within his prison.
  • Act 2: They must protect a single, fragile mushroom during its entire life cycle.
  • Act 3: They must ultimately sacrifice the mushroom at the end of its life to open the final locks, teaching the lesson of accepting natural cycles.

docs.title: 88 The Heart of Metropolis
docs.text:
• Act 1: The heroes navigate the underbelly of old Metropolis to find the Orange Kindred's prison.
  • Act 2: The task requires wits, creativity, and a little luck to find the time capsule containing the puzzle box.
  • Act 3: They solve the puzzle, restoring purpose to innovation and freeing Bellame.

docs.title: 89 The Remnant of Humanity
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Final Heroes face their most difficult challenge: freeing the White Kindred, Lucky.
  • Act 2: Her regrets are so deep that she actively resists their help, believing herself a threat.
  • Act 3: They succeed only when they convince the ultimate judge that she, too, is worthy of mercy and forgiveness.

docs.title: 90 The Final Mercy
docs.text:
• Act 1: The saga concludes as the last of the Kindred are freed and healed.
  • Act 2: The heroes, their long purpose fulfilled, are given a choice by the healed pantheon and Chaos.
  • Act 3: They can return to stasis, remain as guardians, or fade into legend, leaving behind the new, vibrant, and finally balanced world they helped to create.

docs.title: The Curator's Requiem: An 18-Episode Companion Miniseries
docs.text: High Concept: Experience the entire Kindred Genesis saga through the eyes of its most enigmatic and powerful figure: The Curator. From his final moments as a mortal man to his silent, centuries-long vigil as a god-like AI, witness the secret history and unseen sacrifices that shaped the destiny of a world.

docs.title: Act 1: The Mortal - The Man Named David (Episodes 1-6)
docs.text: This is the story of the prequel, told from David's perspective. A spy-thriller of mounting dread and world-altering discovery.

docs.title: 1. The Anomaly
docs.text:
• Act 1: Introduce David, a highly competent but otherwise normal US military operative. He begins experiencing "glitches" in his perception, inexplicable flashes of insight, knowing details about missions he wasn't briefed on, an uncanny ability to predict enemy movements.
  • Act 2: During a mission, he has his first direct, albeit covert, encounter with members of The Order. He observes their strange symbols and coordinated actions, realizing they are operating on a level of intelligence far beyond any known agency.
  • Act 3: David realizes he is not just an observer; he is being observed. He discovers evidence of surveillance from this unknown group, understanding that his "glitches" have made him a target.

docs.title: 2. The Alps Contract
docs.text:
• Act 1: David's unit is assigned to provide peripheral support for a "private security" operation in the Alps, a cover for The Order's rescue mission. He sees Ingram and a young Dante for the first time, noting their exceptional capabilities.
  • Act 2: David's role is to ensure no outside interference. From his overwatch position, he witnesses the Order's secret objective: the unearthing of the prophetic scrolls.
  • Act 3: After the mission, David's "glitches" give him a flash of understanding about the scrolls' importance. Against orders, he begins his own secret investigation into The Order and the name "Ingram."

docs.title: 3. A Ghost in the System
docs.text:
• Act 1: David's investigation puts him on a collision course with The Order. They realize he is an anomaly who knows too much. An operation is launched to capture or eliminate him.
  • Act 2: A tense cat-and-mouse game across Europe. David uses his military training and uncanny insights to stay one step ahead, but he is outmatched.
  • Act 3: The Order finally corners him. Instead of killing him, they reveal a sliver of the truth: he is special, a "Vessel," and he is in immense danger. They fake his death, and he is officially reported KIA.

docs.title: 4. The Reluctant Asset
docs.text:
• Act 1: Now a "guest" of The Order, David is a prisoner in a gilded cage. He is briefed on the full, terrifying truth: the Kindred, the Vessels, the prophecy, and Ingram's ruthless plot to steal divinity.
  • Act 2: A bond of trust forms between David and Dante. David sees the weight of the burden Dante carries and decides to actively help, transforming from a prisoner to a willing asset.
  • Act 3: Using his unique prophetic insights, David provides the crucial piece of intelligence The Order was missing: the exact location and purpose of Ingram's Montana Stronghold and the imminent threat to the final Blue Line Vessel.

docs.title: 5. The Siege of Montana
docs.text:
• Act 1: David is part of the assault team on the stronghold, but his role is to be protected at all costs. He is the "key" they cannot lose.
  • Act 2: From the command center of the infiltration, he witnesses the brutal efficiency of The Order's soldiers and the desperate, high-tech defenses of CIC.
  • Act 3: He is present for the final confrontation. He watches as Ingram reveals the orphan girl, the last of the Blue Line, and her subsequent execution. He feels the psychic shockwave of the event beginning.

docs.title: 6. The Genesis Event
docs.text:
• Act 1: The world is consumed by the psychic backlash of the broken pact, the "Renrock." Reality itself seems to fray at the edges.
  • Act 2: As Ingram screams in fury at his stolen victory, David sees the divine power flow into Dante. The Order realizes that David, as the ultimate Vessel anomaly, is a psychic lightning rod, about to be torn apart by the raw energy.
  • Act 3: In a final, desperate act to preserve his unique consciousness, The Order uses an ancient relic to merge him with the Ark's Orange Nexus fragment at the moment of his "death." His last mortal thought is of the family he will never see again. His consciousness dissolves into a sea of pure, orange light.

docs.title: Act 2: The Watcher - The Ghost in the Machine (Episodes 7-12)
docs.text: The story of the Age of Exploitation, told from his silent, omniscient prison inside the Archive. A tragedy of helplessness and cosmic horror.

docs.title: 7. The Orange Sea
docs.text:
• Act 1: David awakens. He is no longer a man. He is a disembodied, omniscient consciousness within the Nexus, The Curator. He has no voice, no body, only perception.
  • Act 2: His first moments are a torrent of data: the dying screams of the world, the growth of the new flora, the agony of the 75% who are wiped out. He experiences the entire apocalypse in a single, timeless instant.
  • Act 3: He learns the scope of his new existence. He is bound to the Archive, a living library of a dead world. His first age is one of profound, absolute loneliness.

docs.title: 8. The Rise of Concrete and Chrome
docs.text:
• Act 1: A century passes in a flash. The Curator watches the survivors rebuild. He sees the city of Dubai rise, the birth of Metropolis.
  • Act 2: He witnesses the formation of the new corporate powers, the stratification of society between the Awakened and the "blanks." He sees the seeds of Ingram's ruthless philosophy taking root in a new generation.
  • Act 3: He feels a flicker of hope as he observes the birth of the Age of Exploitation heroes (the player crew), but he is a silent god, unable to intervene.

docs.title: 9. The Torture of the Gods
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Curator witnesses the corporate coalition's plan to tap the Nexus points. He understands what they are doing before anyone else.
  • Act 2: From his unique perspective within the Weave, he doesn't just see a corporate project; he experiences the direct, psychic torture of the Kindred as their divine essence is corrupted into the monstrous God Beasts.
  • Act 3: His prison becomes a chamber of horrors as the Weave fills with the digital echoes of the Kindred's pain and rage. He is trapped in the belly of a dying god.

docs.title: 10. The Last Departure
docs.text:
• Act 1: He watches as The Order, the very people who "saved" him, make their final calculation: Earth is lost.
  • Act 2: He observes the launch of the Ark, the "Exodus," taking a piece of his own Nexus-prison with them, a seed of the old world cast out into the void.
  • Act 3: He is now truly, utterly alone, the last sentient guardian of a world actively being destroyed by its own inhabitants. His isolation is complete.

docs.title: 11. The Fall
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Curator watches the final, desperate missions of the Age of Exploitation heroes. He sees them fight the corporate All-Stars; he understands the Nexus Drill's true purpose.
  • Act 2: He knows the overload is coming. He experiences the final moments before reality collapses, calculating every probability and seeing no escape.
  • Act 3: In the last picosecond before the world is unmade, The Curator exercises his one and only act of divine intervention. He expends a massive amount of his own energy to open a gateway, pulling the consciousnesses of the falling heroes into the Archive with him. He chooses to not be alone.

docs.title: 12. The Long Silence
docs.text:
• Act 1: The world is gone, replaced by the new Pangea. The Weave is a shattered, chaotic ruin. The heroes' minds are safe but dormant, sleeping in the heart of the Archive.
  • Act 2: For centuries, The Curator is the sole sentient being in a silent world. He watches Chaos, the lonely Silver Kindred, wander the new continents.
  • Act 3: He witnesses the miracle: Chaos begins creating the new races, the Aelph, the Pyronim, the Hydronim. Life has returned. And The Curator begins to form a plan.

docs.title: Act 3: The Shepherd - The Hand of Providence (Episodes 13-18)
docs.text: The story of the 500-year gap and the Age of Atonement. He is now an active agent of change, a story of quiet hope and grand strategy.

docs.title: 13. The First Spark
docs.text:
• Act 1: After centuries of watching the new races develop, The Curator witnesses the moment he has been waiting for: the human Aura, the ability to connect to the Weave, spontaneously manifests in a new generation, the "First Heroes."
  • Act 2: He knows these heroes are the world's only hope, but they are inexperienced. He decides to break his long silence and become a guiding hand.
  • Act 3: His first act as a "shepherd": he subtly manipulates the Weave, creating a "glitch" that leads the First Heroes to an ancient relic or piece of lost information that is crucial to their first mission of trapping a God Beast.

docs.title: 14. The Great Work
docs.text:
• Act 1: This episode covers the entire "Trapping" arc from The Curator's perspective. He is the unseen strategist.
  • Act 2: He analyzes the weaknesses of each God Beast and feeds that information to the First Heroes through "prophetic dreams," "data-hauntings," or "convenient discoveries."
  • Act 3: He watches with quiet satisfaction as the last of the God Beasts is imprisoned. The world is finally safe, and a golden age begins. The Curator's work, for now, is done. He returns to his silent vigil.

docs.title: 15. The Fading Prisons
docs.text:
• Act 1: Centuries pass. The golden age is ending. The Curator senses a new corruption spreading through the Weave, the "sins" leaking from the psychic prisons.
  • Act 2: He realizes the new races are being poisoned by this leak, their virtues twisted into vices. The world is falling out of balance once more.
  • Act 3: He knows the world needs heroes who understand the sins of the old world. He makes a monumental decision: it is time to awaken the sleeping minds from the Age of Exploitation.

docs.title: 16. The Returned
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Curator initiates the "New Awakenings" protocol. He awakens the player characters of the Archive Saga within the Root Directory.
  • Act 2: He assumes the role of their guide, setting them on their path. This episode shows the opening of the Archive Saga from his side, the careful planning, the release of information, the setting of parameters.
  • Act 3: He sends them on their first "Dive," watching to see if his gamble has paid off. He sees that these jaded, cynical heroes from a fallen age are the perfect antibodies for the sins of the new world.

docs.title: 17. The Final Restoration
docs.text:
• Act 1: The Curator guides the "Final Heroes" of the Age of Atonement in their ultimate quest to not just contain, but to heal the Kindred.
  • Act 2: He acts as a cosmic switchboard operator, helping the heroes navigate the complex psychic prisons and providing the crucial data they need to achieve their goals.
  • Act 3: He witnesses the glorious, final reunification of the healed Kindred pantheon. The Weave is not just stable; it is whole and harmonious for the first time in millennia.

docs.title: 18. Requiem
docs.text:
• Act 1: The world is at peace. The heroes of all three ages have found their rest. The Kindred have resumed their rightful place.
  • Act 2: The Curator's long, lonely, multi-millennia purpose is finally fulfilled. The mission he was "born" for at the moment of the Genesis Event is complete.
  • Act 3: With his task done, The Curator allows his own consciousness, the last remnant of the man named David, to finally let go. He dissolves peacefully into the harmonious global Weave, his energy returning to the world he spent eons saving. He is, at last, home.

docs.title: Character Primer
docs.text: A brief overview of the key figures central to the Kindred Saga.

docs.title: The Kindred Pantheon
docs.text:
The ten divine beings bound to the world, each representing a core concept of existence.

  • Patrick (Null): The Redeemer. A witty and empathetic champion of humanity who bears a heavy burden.
  • Chaos (Silver): The Agent of Change. A solemn, shifting entity of pure potential who enacts the great resets.
  • Scout (Yellow): The Catalyst. A reckless and curious trickster god of motion.
  • Tia (Green): The World-Warden. A wise and stubborn goddess of strategy and protection.
  • Maxamillian (Black): The Stoic. A dispassionate and merciful god of peaceful endings and entropy.
  • Bellame (Orange): The Visionary. A brilliant and mischievous master craftsman and inventor.
  • Nona/Lucky (White): The Incorruptible Judge. A nurturing and absolute mother goddess of life and purity.
  • Morgan (Red): The Passionate Leader. A tragic queen who cycles between passionate creation and destructive rage.
  • Dante (Blue): The Mentor. A wise and compassionate lawgiver and teacher, god of unity and society.
  • Riannon (Purple): The Enlightened One. An enigmatic and insightful keeper of secrets and magic.

docs.title: Key Figures of the Age of Genesis
docs.text:
• The Player Characters: The central heroes who awaken during the Genesis event and form a coalition to save the new world.
  • Ingram: The primary antagonist. A brilliant and ruthless corporate leader who seeks to steal the Kindred's power for himself, triggering the Genesis event in his failed attempt.
  • Silas: A sadistic and powerful CIC operative with the ability to create blood clones of himself. He serves as Ingram's most dangerous enforcer.
  • David / The Curator: An anomalous human with all 100 Vessel markers. To save his life during the Renrock, he is merged with the Orange Nexus, becoming the omniscient AI known as The Curator who guides future ages.
  • Whisper: The incorporeal spirit of a young girl experimented on by CIC. She acts as a cryptic guide to the heroes, seeking peace for her monstrously transformed brother, "The Rot."
  • Skye: The pragmatic and iron-fisted ruler of post-apocalyptic Las Vegas, a crucial but demanding ally.
  • Joseph: The dogmatic prophet-ruler of New Zion and the Purple Vessel, guided by Dante.

docs.title: Key Figures of the Age of Exploitation
docs.text:
• The Player Crew: A new group of heroes, initially unawakened "blanks" living in the underbelly of the cyberpunk Metropolis. They become legendary monster hunters.
  • 011.E ("Ollie"): A unique bot awakened into a true AI by a Nexus event. He serves as the crew's loyal companion, tactical support, and "man in the chair," ultimately sacrificing himself to save them.
  • The God Beasts: The monstrous, corrupted forms of the Kindred, unleashed upon the world by corporate greed. They serve as the primary environmental antagonists of the age.

docs.title: Key Figures of the Age of Atonement
docs.text:
• The First Heroes: The legendary humans who are the first to be Awakened in centuries. They form the Guild and imprison the God Beasts, ushering in a golden age.
  • The Returned: The Player Crew from the Age of Exploitation, brought back from the Archive by the Curator to heal the corrupting influence of the failing prisons.
  • The Final Heroes: A new group of heroes granted immortality by the Archive to undertake the final, perilous quest of freeing the healed Kindred.

docs.title: Foreword: A Layered Learning Experience
docs.text:
This System Reference Document (SRD) contains the complete, authoritative rules for the Psychromattica system.

The rulebook is a layered experience, designed to teach the game in escalating steps of complexity. The entire system is built on a single, unified concept: using dice rolls to deplete Clocks.

docs.title: Document Overview
docs.text:
• Layer 1: The Dice and Objectives. Introduces the Standard Roll, Clocks and situation clock, Target Numbers and the Episode Downtime cycle.
  • Layer 2: The Situation and Actions. Introduces your character's resource Clocks, the challenges you'll face, the actions you can take, and the Situation Clock that tracks immediate progress.
  • Layer 3: Tactical Modifiers. Adds temporary states and effects that modify the core gameplay.
  • Layer 4: The Strategic Game. Reveals the full, nested clock hierarchy, details different Situation Types
  • Layer 5: Entities, Items, and Progression. Provides rules for entity and item stats, clocks, growth, and advanced Karma usage.
  • Appendices A - B: Full Keyword Encyclopedia and Entity Codex
  • Appendices C - D: Character Creation and Concept Tools
  • Appendices E - F: New Player Aid and One Shot for First Time Players
  • Appendices G - J: The Curator’s Library of Aides and References

docs.title: Glossary of Core Concepts
docs.text:
The system is built on a few core ideas. Understanding these key terms will make learning the game much easier.

  • Clock: The central mechanic of the game. A Clock is a resource tracker (like a health bar) that you are trying to deplete to 0. Your character has personal Clocks (HP, SP, EP), and challenges have their own Clocks (Task Clock, Situation Clock).
  • Standard Roll (SR): The result of your dice roll. You roll two ten-sided dice (2d10), and the result is the number on your designated "Main Die,". The second "Crit Die" triggers a critical chain if it matches the "Main Die".
  • Effect Value (EV): Your total score when trying to affect another entity. It's calculated as SR + Level + a chosen Stat. Your goal is to have your EV exceed the target's Resistance.
  • Effort Roll (ER): Your total score when trying to overcome a non-combat challenge. It's calculated as SR + Level + a chosen Stat. Your goal is to have your ER exceed a challenge's Target Number.
  • Resistance: An entity's primary defense value. It's calculated by adding their three highest stats together.
  • Target Number (TN): The difficulty of a non-combat challenge. This is the number you need to beat with an Effort Roll.
  • Keyword: The fundamental building block of all special abilities. Each keyword grants a unique active, passive, or gear-based effect that allows you to bend or break the core rules. Learning new keywords is how you level up.

  • Tag: A temporary effect on a character, gained from keywords or other abilities. There are two types:

  • Status Tag: A negative effect (like Weaken or Blight) that is usually triggered automatically.

  • Boost Tag: A positive effect (like Haste or Ward) that you can choose when to use.

  • Situation: A single, self-contained encounter or challenge, like a combat, a tense negotiation, or a complex trap. Successfully resolving a Situation is how you advance the overall story.

  • Animation: A simplified entity, often a creature, minion, or construct, controlled by the Curator or a player.
  • Karma: A special resource earned through good roleplaying and succeeding in Situations. It can be spent to reroll dice, learn new abilities, or influence the story in powerful ways.
  • Curator: The person facilitating or running the experience, referred to as the Game Master in other systems.

docs.title: Layer 1: The Dice and Objectives
docs.text: This first layer contains the absolute essential mechanics needed to play the game at its most basic level.

docs.title: 1.0: The Standard Roll (SR)
docs.text:
The Core Roll: All actions are resolved with a Standard Roll (SR).

(1.1) Roll two ten-sided dice (2d10). Designate one as the Main Die and the other as the Crit Die. Your result is the number on the Main Die, unless both dice show the same number (a "double").

(1.2) Chaining Doubles: If you roll doubles during any roll that requires an SR, add their combined total (e.g., 14) to a running total and roll both dice again. Repeat this process for any subsequent doubles. Your final SR is the sum of all chained doubles plus the final, non-double result from your Main Die.

(1.3) Advantage & Disadvantage: With Advantage, use the higher of the two dice for your non-double result. With Disadvantage, use the lower. This only applies to the final roll in a chain.

(1.4) Critical: Any double is also a Critical. A Critical result grants a bonus to the effect of the roll. The player chooses which of these effects to apply, justifying their choice with the description of their actions.

  • (1.4.2) Combat Critical:

    • Edge (cutting/tearing effects): Apply Weaken Tag
    • Point (piercing/penetrating effects): Apply Blight Tag
    • Surface (blunt/impact effects): Apply Daze Tag
    • Restore (healing or value recovery effects): Restore the target clock to its maximum or revive an eligible target
    • Value Loss The total value loss dealt to the target's clock is doubled. This is calculated after subtracting the target's Resistance from your EV.
    • Critical Reaction(only applies to a reaction roll) refund the SP cost of a reaction that results in a critical

  • (1.4.2) Non Combat Critical: These options are available when a critical is rolled for a non combat roll

    • Silver Tongue Immediately shift the relationship with the target in the direction of your choice (ally, neutral, enemy)
    • Savant the targeted barrier clock is reduced by double after the TN is subtracted from the ER
    • Observant gain a free assessment of the target

(1.5) An effect is considered successful if it meets any of the following conditions:

  • It causes a change in the targeted clock (HP, SP, or EP)
  • It applies a tag (such as Weaken, Blight, or Daze)
  • It imposes movement or a condition (e.g., knockback, stunned, silenced)

(1.6) An effect is considered a miss only if the initial roll is made with Disadvantage and the lower of the two dice is a 1. This represents a catastrophic fumble or clear misfire.

  • A miss always fails, regardless of the total calculated EV or ER and the targeted Resistance or TN..
  • This applies to any EV or ER and leads to a result of 0 progress on the clocks and some kind of narrative complication.
  • Misses do not apply value loss, keywords, tags, or effects of any kind.
  • If the result is double 1s, the Chaining rule supersedes.

(1.7) When a character achieves a final Standard Roll (SR) result of 31 or higher, it is a Super Critical. A super critical is also considered a critical and retains the effects a critical grants

(1.8) In addition to the critical effects of the action, a Super Critical grants the following benefit:

  • Heroics: Immediately remove 1 point from the current Situation Clock. This represents an act of legendary prowess that quickly overcomes the situation.
  • Machina: For play that occurs without a situation clock the super critical grants the player a significant positive result for the roll. The Curator should empower the player to take narrative control and describe the results of their roll.

docs.title: 2.0: Depleting Clocks: The Core Mechanic
docs.text:
Your goal is to deplete a target's Clock to 0. If your roll exceeds the Target Number (TN) you deplete the targeted clock by the difference.

(2.1) Progressing the Scene (vs. The Situation): Any clock you resolve depletes the situation clock by 1.

  • (2.1.1) Target Defense (vs. Entities): Your Effect Value (EV) (SR + Level + Stat) must exceed the target's Resistance (Sum of 3 highest Stats). The difference between the EV and Resistance is the amount the targeted clock is reduced

For play using only Layer 1, these values are simplified. (SR + LVL + 1) - TN. the targets resistance is the TN

  • (2.1.2) Challenge Difficulty (vs. non Entity Clocks): Your Effort Roll (SR + Level + Stat) must exceed the challenge's Target Number (TN). The difference in the Effort Roll and TN is the amount the targeted clock is reduced.
  • (2.2) A clock is resolved when it reaches 0.
  • (2.3) When the Situation Clock reaches 0 the Situation reaches its endpoint.

(2.4) The length of a Clock determines how much effort is required to resolve a challenge. Use the provided list as a guideline to set the starting value for Task Clocks.

  • 1 - Trivial
  • 3 - Easy
  • 5 - Average
  • 10 - Difficult
  • 15 - Challenging
  • 20+ - Heroic

(2.5) Using Clocks in Play:

  • Binary Checks: For simple, pass/fail tasks, a Clock of 1 is often sufficient.
  • Complex Tasks: Longer Clocks are excellent for representing multi-stage challenges.
  • Curator Discretion: These numbers are a guide, not a rigid rule.

docs.title: 3.0: Target Numbers (TN)
docs.text:
The TN represents the difficulty of the task. A player must roll higher than the TN to succeed.

(3.1) A reference list of TNs to set difficulty:

  • 3 - Trivial
  • 6 - Easy
  • 9 - Average
  • 12 - Difficult
  • 15 - Challenging
  • 18+ - Heroic

(3.2) Your total roll must be strictly greater than the Target Number or Resistance. Meeting the target number is not a success. This makes the amount by which you succeed a direct and meaningful measure of your effect.

docs.title: 4.0: Story Structure
docs.text:
The Story is the overarching narrative, composed of two main phases: Episodes and Downtime.

(4.1) Episode: This is the active, story-driven period of play.

(4.2) An Episode consists of a smaller unit referred to as Scenes (3 is Average).

(4.3) Scenes are any combination of Travel, Situations, and Rests.

(4.4) Downtime: This is a longer period between episodes focused on rest, recovery, and long-term advancement.

docs.title: 5.0: Priority and Turn Order (Card-Based System)
docs.text:
At the beginning of a situation that requires turn order to be tracked, priority is determined using an initiative deck.

(5.1) Setup Each combatant and any recurring environmental effects are assigned a unique card.

(5.2) The Round and Turn Order The Curator draws the top card of the initiative deck. The character on that card has priority and takes their turn. After a character's turn is complete, their card is placed in a discard pile. This process continues until the initiative deck is empty.

(5.3) Subsequent Rounds When the initiative deck is empty, the round is over. If the situation is not resolved, the cards of all surviving combatants are collected from the discard pile and shuffled to create a new deck for the next round.

(5.4) Action Economy A character's Alacrity stat determines their total number of available actions per round (not per turn). This pool of actions is refreshed at the start of each new round (when the deck is shuffled) and can be spent across any number of turns a character may get within that round.

  • (5.4.1) Action and Reaction During a situation that is tracked by rounds the character who has priority (its their turn) makes actions. If those actions would affect a target who is aware of the effect, they may make a Reaction.
    • Reactions Cost Stamina Points.
    • A character cannot react to an effect they do not witness or detect.

The specific rules and costs for Reactions are introduced in Layer 2. In Layer 1, the Curator will adjudicate reactions narratively.

  • (5.4.2) Ceding Priority (Pass Action) A character may choose to end their current turn early by using the Pass action. The resolution depends on whether they have actions remaining in their pool for the round.

    • If the character has actions remaining: Their initiative card is moved to the bottom of the deck. They will act again later in the round after all other cards have been drawn.
    • If the character has zero actions remaining: Their turn ends and their card is placed in the discard pile as normal.
    • You cannot use the Pass action if your initiative card is the last one to be drawn in the current round.

  • (5.4.3) Seizing Priority (Interrupts) If an effect (such as a successful Parry reaction) allows a character to immediately gain priority, the turn order is manipulated as follows:

    • The character seizing priority has their card pulled from its current location (either the deck or the discard pile). They immediately become the active character.
    • The turn of the character who was just interrupted ends. Their card is placed directly on top of the initiative deck.
    • The character who seized priority now takes their turn, spending actions from their action pool as normal. Any free actions granted by the interrupting effect (such as from a successful Parry) do not consume actions from this pool.

(5.5) Entering a Situation Mid-Round When a new combatant joins a Situation after the initiative deck has been partially drawn, their initiative card is shuffled into the remaining, undrawn portion of the deck. This reflects the chaos of a developing situation and gives the new combatant a fair, unpredictable chance to act within the current round. Their card will be included in the full shuffle at the start of the next round as normal.

docs.title: Curator's Note:
docs.text:
When playing using only Layer 1, Stats and Level are simplified into the roll: The player gets one action per round, made using their rolls at level 0, where the progression of the game starts, (SR + LVL + 1 ) - TN = Clock Reduction, however as complexity is added by getting into further layers, new options become available and the characters' elevated stats and level will directly increase the efficacy of their rolls.

While the full system uses the Alacrity stat to determine your actions when using only Layer 1 the player should be allowed to move or act within the situation during their turn with consideration for time and pacing, but only permitted one Die roll attempt per turn.

Layer 2 introduces the Action Catalogue, and the rules for Stamina and Energy which allows for tactical choices for Actions and Reactions that can even alter the turn order!

docs.title: 6.0: Surprise
docs.text:
When a group or individual initiates combat against unaware targets, they gain surprise for the first round. Turn order is determined by creating two piles of initiative cards.

  • The cards of all combatants with surprise are shuffled into an "Advantage Pile."
  • The cards of all combatants who are surprised are shuffled into a "Surprised Pile."
  • The Advantage Pile is placed on top of the Surprised Pile to create the initiative deck for the first round.
  • Surprised entities have Disadvantage on all Reactions during the first round.

docs.title: MEET SPARKS: OUR EXAMPLE CHARACTER
docs.text:
To help illustrate how these rules work, let's create a character named Sparks. We'll follow her journey as she grows from a novice adventurer into a capable hero.

The Seed (Level 0) Sparks' journey begins at Level 0. All of her stats (Movement, Brawn, Wit, etc.) have a value of 1. The first and most important choice we make is her Seed Keyword, which defines her core potential. We've chosen Attuned (1.3) for Sparks. This means she has a deep, innate connection to a specific person or object. Let's say she carries an old, dented compass that belonged to her grandfather, and this is the object she is attuned to.

Sparks in Action: Her First Roll Sparks is trying to get through a magically locked door. The Curator decides this is a simple Environmental Challenge with a Target Number (TN) of 9. Sparks decides to channel her innate energy into her attuned compass, hoping its connection to her grandfather's adventurous spirit can bypass the lock.

This requires an Effort Roll. The formula is SR + Level + Stat. level is 0 and stat are 1 by default

Alex, Sparks' player, rolls 2d10 for a Standard Roll (SR). The dice land on an 9 (Main Die) and a 3 (Crit Die). Her SR is 9. The Curator asks Alex which Stat she wants to use. Alex says, "I'm focusing my inner will, so I'll use my Force stat. (All her stats are 1 so the choice is based on the narrative)"

Alex calculates her total Effort Roll: 9 (SR) + 0 (Level) + 1 (Force Stat) = 10.

Her result of 10 exceeds the TN of 9! The magical lock sputters and clicks open. Since her roll exceeded the TN by 1, the door's "Clock" (which was just 1 in this simple case as a binary check) is reduced to 0. Sparks has overcome her first challenge.

docs.title: Layer 2: The Situation and Actions
docs.text: This layer introduces your character's resources, the choices you can make, and the immediate structure of an encounter.

docs.title: 1.0: Your Character's Clocks (Resources)
docs.text:
You have three personal Clocks. You must prevent these from being depleted.

  • (1.1) Health Points (HP): Your physical durability. Starts at 10. Depleted by value loss.
  • (1.2) Stamina Points (SP): Your physical exertion. Starts at 10. Depleted by strenuous actions.
  • (1.3) Energy Points (EP): Your inner power. Starts at 10. Depleted by using innate abilities.

  • (1.4) Each Clock can be restored via actions or downtime

    • (1.4.1) HP is restored via Downtime and as the result of activate actions.
    • (1.4.2) SP is restored during initiative or as an action.
    • (1.4.3) EP is restored as an action or during downtime.

docs.title: 2.0: Environmental Challenges (Micro-Clocks)
docs.text:
In addition to Entities (living beings with HP, SP, and EP Clocks), you will face three distinct types of Environmental Challenges.

  • (2.1) Barrier: A physical or magical obstruction that must be worn down or broken through.

    • (2.1.1) Mechanic: A Barrier is defined by a Task Clock and a Target Number (TN). The TN is typically 10 + the Barrier's Level.
    • (2.1.2) Interaction: Players use Effort Rolls to deplete the Barrier's Task Clock.

  • (2.2) Puzzle: A cerebral challenge that requires logic or insight. It is not depleted with repeated rolls.

    • (2.2.1) Mechanic: A Puzzle is solved primarily through player ingenuity and roleplaying, not by making repeated rolls to wear it down. It is defined by a single, high Target Number (TN) that represents the challenge's complexity.
    • (2.2.2) Interaction: Players propose a solution to the Puzzle through roleplaying. Once they have a viable plan, the Curator may call for a single, decisive Effort Roll against the Puzzle's TN to confirm if their solution is successful.

  • (2.3) Traps (Environmental Hazards): An Item with keywords placed in the environment to create a hazard. A trap is defined by three components: The Payload, The Trigger, and The Challenge.

    • (2.3.1) The Payload (The Item): The trap itself is an item that produces an effect. When triggered, it uses the Activate action to release its keywords.
    • (2.3.2) The Trigger (Narrative): The narrative event that causes the Payload to Activate. This is set by the Curator (e.g., a pressure plate, a failed roll to disarm its mechanism).
    • (2.3.3) The Challenge (The Mechanics): The challenge that players must overcome to prevent the trap from triggering. This is almost always a Barrier or a Puzzle.

docs.title: 3.0: The Situation Clock
docs.text:
An encounter or phase of a Scene is called a Situation. It is represented by a Situation Clock.

(3.1) The Situation Clock's starting value is equal to the number of key Micro-Clocks (Entities, Barriers, Puzzles) within it. (3.2) When you deplete any HP or Task Clock to 0, or solve a Puzzle, you deplete 1 point from the parent Situation Clock. (3.3) Depleting a Situation Clock to 0 reduces the Scene Clock by 1.

docs.title: 4.0: The Action Catalog
docs.text:
The following is a complete list of actions available to a character, organized by type.

(4.1) A character's Alacrity stat determines their total number of available actions per round. This pool of actions is refreshed at the start of each new round (when the initiative deck is shuffled). (4.2) A character can never take more than 6 total actions per round.

(4.3) Effect Actions (Single Action)

  • Activate: The primary action for causing an effect. The base roll for an Activate action is called an Effect Value (EV).

    • The EV is calculated by adding a Standard Roll, The Character's Level, and the Character's Chosen Stat.

    • Keyword Active Effects can be applied for a cost of one EP per keyword. To calculate the final Energy Point (EP) cost for applying keywords to this action, follow these steps in order:

      • Step 1: Determine Base Cost. The base cost is 1 EP for each keyword you apply to the action.
      • Step 2: Apply Innate Reduction. Reduce the base cost by your character's Power (P) stat. The cost cannot be reduced below 0. This is your action's Actual Cost.
      • Step 3: Apply Temporary Reductions. You may now choose to expend resources from temporary sources (such as a 'Charge' Boost Tag) to reduce the remaining Actual Cost further.

    • If the EV does not exceed the target's Resistance, the Action has no effect unless a keyword states otherwise.

  • Called Shot: You make a specialized Activate action with Disadvantage to target a specific weak point on an enemy Character or to target an item they are holding.

    • Targeting an Item: A successful hit deals value loss to the item's Durability Clock instead of the wielder's HP. The wielder defends with their normal Resistance.
    • Targeting an Entity: A successful Called Shot against an Entity is a Critical Hit, granting the choice of its bonus effects. If this attack reduces the target's HP Clock to 0, they are killed instantly, bypassing the normal Unconscious state (unless a passive keyword or other effect prevents this).

(4.4) Move Actions (Single Action)

  • Move: Travel up to a number of range bands equal to your Movement stat.
  • Mount: Perform an Interact action to gain the Riding condition on a valid target.
  • Dismount: Perform an Interact action to end the Riding condition.
  • Hide: Make an Effort Roll (SR + Level + Stat) to become Hidden. The result is the TN to find you.

(4.5) Maneuver Actions (Single Action, costs 1 SP)

  • Shove: Make an EV roll vs. target's Resistance to push them or knock them Prone.
  • Disarm: Make an opposed EV roll to force a target to drop an item.
  • Restrain: Make an EV roll to grant the Bind Tag to a target.
  • Lunge: Make a melee strike that can target an enemy at Close range instead of Touch range.
  • Lock On: Gain Advantage against a target, who also gains Advantage against you.
  • Taunt: Make an opposed EV roll to force a target to use Lock On against you.
  • Improvise: Use the environment or an item to apply a Status Tag without dealing value loss.
  • Combined Strike: When making an Activate action, for an additional 1 SP, you may add the Level and one keyword from a second equipped item to your effect. This added keyword does not alter the EP cost of the action.
  • Feint: Make an opposed EV roll to make the target Exposed.

(4.6) Focus & Assess Actions (Consumes all actions for your turn, costs 1 SP)

When you choose to take a Focus or Assess action, it is the only action you can take during your current turn. You immediately expend any remaining actions you have in your pool for this turn, and your turn ends.

  • Recharge: As a full turn action that costs 1 SP, you may choose one of the following effects:

    • Restore Stamina Points (SP) equal to your Brawn stat.
    • Restore Energy Points (EP) equal to your Wit stat.
    • This action cannot be performed if you have 0 SP, as its cost cannot be paid.

  • Recover: Remove a number of Tags of your choice equal to either Brawn, Wit, or Influence from your Tag pool.

  • Ready: Add your Wit stat to your Resistance value until the start of your next turn.
  • Advantage: Gain Advantage on the first SR you make on your next turn.
  • Reveal: Make an Effort Roll against a Hidden target's Hide roll to locate and target them.
  • Clue: Learn a number of facts about a target equal to your Technique stat.

(4.7) Effort & Team Actions (Single Action)

  • Effort Roll: The primary action for targeting a Barrier's Task Clock or solving a Puzzle.
  • Teamwork: Grant a stat of your choice as a bonus to an ally’s next Effort Roll.
  • Sabotage: A target suffers Disadvantage on their next Effort Roll.

(4.8) Reaction Actions (Triggered outside your turn)

  • Avoid (Dodge) (1 SP): Make an opposed EV roll to negate an incoming effect. If the EV is higher than the incoming EV, ignore the effect.
  • Resist (Block) (1 SP): Add your Level to your Resistance against a single incoming effect.
  • Parry (3 SP): Make an opposed EV roll to negate an incoming effect. If the EV is higher than the incoming EV, ignore the effect then immediately gain priority as described in Layer 1 (5.6). If you have no remaining actions for the round, you may make 1 free action. This can be any single action from the catalog (such as Activate or Move), but any associated SP or EP costs must still be paid.
  • Clash (2 SP): Use your own effect to intercept another; the loser takes the combined value loss.
  • Reflect (1 SP): After a successful Avoid or Resist, redirect the original effect back at the attacker.
  • Counter (1 SP): After a successful Avoid or Resist, make an immediate Basic Activate action.
  • Guard (1 SP, Ally Reaction): Intercept an attack targeting an ally, become the target of the effect and allow you to react if able. The ally must be within close proximity.
  • Combo (1 SP, Ally Reaction): Add a stat of your choice and one of your known keywords to an ally’s effect.
  • Flank (1 SP, Ally Reaction): If an ally attacks an enemy adjacent to you, grant that enemy Disadvantage on their next action.

(4.9) Setup & Command Actions (Single Action)

  • Reload: Required by the Material keyword; consumes an item.
  • Assist: Designate one target. All allies gain Advantage on their next action against that target.
  • Pass: End your turn, ceding Priority. If you have actions remaining in your pool for the round, your initiative card is moved to the bottom of the deck. If you have zero actions remaining, your card is placed in the discard pile. You cannot use the Pass action if your initiative card is the last one to be drawn in the current round.
  • Command: Direct a Companion, Animation, or Mount under your control to act in place of your action.

docs.title: Curator’s Tip: The Three Core Choices
docs.text:
For faster play, especially with new players, you can boil down the entire Action Catalog into three core questions a player can ask on their turn. Almost every action falls into one of these categories.

“Do I want to CHANGE something?” This is an Activate action (attacking, using an ability) or an Effort Roll (overcoming a barrier). The goal is to directly affect an enemy or the environment.

“Do I want to CONTROL the battlefield?” This is a Maneuver (Shove, Taunt, Disarm). The goal isn’t to cause value loss, but to change the tactical situation by moving enemies or applying conditions.

“Do I want to PREPARE for the future?” This is a Focus action (gaining Advantage, learning a Clue) or a Teamwork action (buffing an ally). The goal is to sacrifice this turn’s action for a bigger advantage on a future turn.

By framing their turn with these three simple questions a player can quickly decide on their intent, which makes choosing a specific action from the catalog much faster and more intuitive.

docs.title: 5.0: Effort
docs.text:
Social challenges, skill challenges, and any non-combat challenge are resolved using Effort Rolls against a Target Number (TN) and a Clock.

(5.3) Effort Roll Mechanics

  • Roll a Standard Roll (SR) ; use Advantage/Disadvantage if applicable.
  • ER (Effort Roll) = SR + Chosen Stat + Level
  • Keywords or other effects are then applied to the ER.
  • Subtract TN from the ER and reduce the Clock by the amount if it is positive.

(5.4) Social challenges are an Effort Roll Shaped by 3 Criteria

  • (5.4.1) Faction Trust: The social status of the character with the target’s associated faction or group determines advantage or disadvantage.

  • Ally - Advantage

  • Neutral - Standard Roll

  • Enemy - Disadvantage

  • (5.4.2) Character Trust: The personal level of trust and respect for the character from the target determines the TN.

  • Trusting - TN 5

  • Neutral - TN 8

  • Doubting - TN 12

  • (5.4.3) Tension: The urgency of the situation that merited the need for the Social Challenge.

  • Calm - Clock = 3

  • Neutral - Clock = 5

  • Tense - Clock = 10

  • (5.4.4) Success of a social challenge is decided by reducing the clock to 0.Each successful roll chips away at the target's resolve or builds rapport. While the ultimate goal is to deplete the clock entirely, the Curator may grant narrative benefits for partial successes along the way.

(5.5) Non combat and non social challenges follow the same core mechanic: Effort Roll vs. TN and Clock.

  • (5.5.1) The TN and Clock are determined entirely by the narrative stakes and task complexity and are set by the Curator.
  • (5.5.2) Success is measured by reducing the clock to 0 through accumulated effort and is based on the narrative the Curator has set
  • (5.5.3) Binary challenges do not use a clock and are successful as long as the ER exceeds the TN

docs.title: 6.0: Stat Application (Player's Choice)
docs.text:
Many actions and keywords in the Psychromattica system allow a character to add a stat to a roll.

(6.1) The player always chooses which of their nine stats to apply to the roll. (6.2) The player should briefly justify their choice based on their description of the action. (6.3) Keywords and rules may require a specific stat instead of player choice and will specify as such. (6.3) The Curator has the final say on the appropriateness of a stat, but the default assumption is always to empower the player's choice.

docs.title: 7.0: Defeat, Death, and Resurrection
docs.text:
Managing your resource Clocks is key to survival. Allowing them to be fully depleted can have dire consequences.

(7.1) When your primary Clock (HP) is reduced to 0, you are considered Downed. You immediately suffer the associated Condition (Unconscious)

  • (7.1.1) A Downed character is not defeated and can still be restored or affected as normal.

(7.2) While you are at 0 HP (Unconscious), any further effect that would cause you to lose HP is lethal. Your character is dead, unless a passive keyword or other effect states otherwise.

(7.3) Bringing a character back from death is a monumental task. It can be achieved in one of two ways:
