docs.title: Character Creation Guide (The Focused Awakening)
docs.text:
Welcome! You are an "Awakened" character, starting at Level 1 with four unique abilities.

Step 1: Choose Your Seed Keyword Pick one Archetype from the list above. This is your core identity and your Seed Keyword.

Step 2: Find Your Trinity Color Palette Your Seed Keyword has a color. Find that color on the Wheel of Change below. Your "Trinity Palette" is that color and its two neighbors. Example: If your Seed is Sturdy (Green), your palette is Yellow, Green, and White.

Step 3: Choose Your Awakening Keywords You now learn three more keywords, one from each color in your Trinity Palette. This gives you a curated list of ~27 thematic abilities to choose from. * One keyword from your Seed color's list. * One keyword from the left neighbor's list. * One keyword from the right neighbor's list.

you could also choose all three keywords from the seed keywords color, or a simple hybrid build of 2 keywords that share a color with the seed and one keyword from either of the neighboring colors for more focused builds.

Step 4: Apply Your Trinity Stat Bonus * All nine of your stats start with a baseline of 2. * You get +3 bonus points, one for the stat associated with each of your three Trinity colors.

Step 5: Design Your Signature Item Describe one piece of gear and choose any one keyword for it from the full Master Keyword List. This does not have to be from your Trinity Palette. (this can be random rolled as well, reroll any flaw keywords)

Step 6: Calculate Final Values * HP: 10 * Resistance: Add your three highest stats together.

docs.title: Reference: The Wheel of Change
docs.text: Silver -> Red -> Black -> Purple -> Yellow -> Green -> White -> Orange -> Blue -> Silver

docs.title: Reference: Color / Stat Association
docs.text:
• Silver (1): Movement
  • Yellow (2): Alacrity
  • Green (3): Brawn
  • Black (4): Wit
  • Orange (5): Expertise
  • White (6): Technique
  • Red (7): Power
  • Blue (8): Influence
  • Purple (9): Force
  • Null (0): Any (Player's Choice)

docs.title: Running the Game (Curator's Cheat Sheet)
docs.text:
• The Roll: ER = SR (d10 Main Die) + Level (1) + Chosen Stat.
  • The Goal: Beat the Target Number (TN) to deplete Clocks.
  • Keywords: Players use the full text of their four innate keywords. Encourage creative use! Using keywords is free for the one-shot.
  • Item Keyword: Provides a passive benefit when the item is used.
  • Criticals: Doubles = double depletion.
  • Damage: If an enemy roll > player's Resistance, they lose HP equal to the difference.

docs.title: 1.0 Game Objective
docs.text: The goal of Psychromattica is to reduce the opposing Player's Health Points (HP) from 10 to 0. This is achieved by placing 10 or more damage markers on their Player Mat.

docs.title: 2.1 Game Zones
docs.text:
• Personal Zones: A Player's Hand, their In-Play Units, their Personal Codex deck, and a designated Active Keyword Blocks Area on the Player Mat.

    • About the Player Mat

      The Player Mat contains the Player unit card, their active Codex Cards, equipped Item Cards, and any Tags. It also has designated trackers for Energy (EN) and Karma.
  • Communal Zones: The Main Deck and the Discard Pile are shared by all Players.

docs.title: 2.2 Unit
docs.text: A "Unit" is any entity in the game that can be targeted, damaged, and destroyed. This includes a Player (represented by their Player card) and any Animation cards in play.

docs.title: 2.3 Keyword Structure
docs.text:
Keywords are designated by a two-part number (e.g., C.D where C is Color and D is Category).

  • The first digit (C) represents the keyword's Color Code (0-9).
  • The second digit (.D) represents its Category, defining its thematic role and function:
    • .0: Flaw (Typically detrimental or impose a cost/restriction)
    • .1: Gift (Often innate, beneficial passive or active abilities)
    • .2: Talent (Learned skills or proficiencies)
    • .3: Quirk (Unusual or specific minor abilities)
    • .4: Boost (Typically apply beneficial Boost Tags or positive effects)
    • .5: Status (Typically apply detrimental or conditional Status Tags)
    • .6: Form (Relate to the shape, area, or delivery method of an effect)
    • .7: Modifier (Alter how an effect or action works)
    • .8: Drive (Represent a style, approach, or potent offensive capability)
    • .9: Unique (Often powerful, signature, or reality-altering abilities)

docs.title: 2.4 Keyword Blocks
docs.text:
The game features 50 unique Keyword Blocks. Each Color (0-9) has five distinct Keyword Blocks, each represented by a physical Codex Card. A Keyword Block consists of a pair of keywords from the same Color, based on their Category:

  • Block Type 1: Keywords #.1 & #.2
  • Block Type 2: Keywords #.3 & #.4
  • Block Type 3: Keywords #.5 & #.6
  • Block Type 4: Keywords #.7 & #.8
  • Block Type 5: Keywords #.9 & #.0

When a Player unlocks a Keyword Block, they gain access to both keywords on that Codex Card for Player Keyword Augmentation.

docs.title: 2.5 The Guardian Precedence
docs.text: A Player cannot be targeted by an Attack or Critical Strike action if that Player controls one or more Animations. The Animations must be dealt with first.

docs.title: 2.6 Action Economy
docs.text:
• Each Animation may take one (1) action per turn.
  • Each Player can take two (2) actions per turn.

An entity that has taken an action is considered "spent." A spent Animation is turned sideways. A Player places one Player Spent Token on their mat for each action taken. A Player may end their turn at any point except in the middle of resolving an action.

docs.title: 2.7 System Refresh
docs.text: At the end of each Player's turn, that Player's hand size is set to exactly 5 by either drawing or discarding.

docs.title: 2.8 The Perpetual Library
docs.text: If a Player must draw or reveal a card from the Main Deck and it is empty, the communal Discard Pile is immediately shuffled to become the new Main Deck. The action is then completed.

docs.title: 2.9 Damage & Destruction
docs.text: Damage is tracked with damage markers. A unit is destroyed when the number of damage markers on it is equal to or greater than its Power.

docs.title: 2.10 The Suppressed State
docs.text:
To show a unit is Suppressed, flip its card face down. A Suppressed unit: * Cannot perform any actions. * Has its printed and equipped keywords inactivated. * Does not count for the Guardian Precedence. * Can be targeted but takes no damage. * Can still receive tags. * Does not ready during the Ready Phase.

To remove the Suppressed state, spend 1 Karma to perform the Re-engage action or use a Liberate Tag.

docs.title: 2.11 Unit Item Limits
docs.text:
• Animations: May have a maximum of one (1) Item equipped.
  • Player: May have a maximum number of Items equipped equal to their current Focus stat.

docs.title: 2.12 Command Limit
docs.text: A Player's Focus stat determines the maximum number of Animations they can command. A Player can control a number of Animations up to, but not exceeding, their current Focus stat.

docs.title: 2.13 Keyword Activation Principle
docs.text:
• Innate Keywords: Printed directly on an Animation's card. They are automatically active when the Animation performs an action and do not count towards any limit.
  • Augmented Keywords: Gained from an external source (e.g., equipped Item, Player's Codex). The number of Augmented keywords a unit can use for a single action is limited by its own Focus stat.

docs.title: 2.14 Deployment State
docs.text: An Animation that enters play is considered 'spent' for that turn and cannot act unless an effect (e.g., Haste) specifically allows it.

docs.title: 2.15 First Turn Restriction
docs.text: During the first turn of the game, the starting player cannot perform the Attack or Critical Strike actions.

docs.title: 2.16 Defensive Sacrifice
docs.text: During the Defender Reaction step, a player may choose to destroy one Item equipped to the defending unit. If they do, that Item's Power value is added to the defending unit's RV for this combat. The destroyed Item is placed in the Discard Pile.

docs.title: 2.17 Keyword Precedence: The Golden Rules
docs.text:
When interpreting card effects, these rules take precedence over all others.

  1. "Can't" Supersedes "Can" If an effect states that something cannot happen, it overrides any effect that says it can. A prohibition always wins.

  2. Specific Overrides General A keyword that defines a complete, alternative resolution process (e.g., Snap, Reckless) takes precedence over keywords that only modify a part of the standard process (e.g., Ranged).

  3. Absolute Effects & Redirection Keywords with definitive language ("cannot be prevented," "instead of," "is unaffected by") create absolute exceptions that supersede standard rules.

  4. Cumulative Effects Unless they directly contradict, multiple non-exclusive effects that trigger from the same event are cumulative. All such effects are applied.

  5. The Actor Principle (Source of an Action) The entity that becomes "spent" to perform an action is the primary actor. This entity pays all costs, is targeted by retaliatory effects, and is referenced by keywords like "the attacker," even if another unit's stats were used.

  6. The Principle of Action Sovereignty The entity performing an action is the sole determinant of which and how many augmented keywords it can use, limited by its own Focus stat. A Player cannot lend their Focus or personal keyword access to an Animation's action.

docs.title: 3.1 Components
docs.text:
• Player Mat (for tracking HP, EN, Focus, Karma)
  • The Faction Pool (20x 10-card Faction Modules)
  • The Codex Pool (50x Codex Cards)
  • Tokens (Damage, Karma, Tags)
  • Player Spent Tokens (2 per player)

docs.title: 3.2 The World Weaving Phase (Main Deck Creation)
docs.text:
1. The Pool: Place all 20 Faction Module decks in the center of the table.
  2. Player Draft: Players roll a d10; the highest roller is first. In turn order, each player chooses one Faction Module until the limit is reached:
    • 2 Players: Each picks 5 modules.
    • 3 Players: Each picks 3 modules (9 total).
    • 4 Players: Each picks 2 modules (8 total).
  3. The Chaos Slot(s): Shuffle the remaining Faction Modules and draw randomly to complete the deck of 10.
  4. Final Assembly: Shuffle the 10 chosen Faction Modules together. This is the shared Main Deck.

docs.title: 3.3 Player Setup
docs.text:
1. Each Player takes a Player Mat. Set HP to 10, EN to 10, and Focus to 1.
  2. Each Player chooses a Primary Color and takes that color's Keyword Block Type 1 Codex Card (keywords #.1 & #.2). Place this in their Active Keyword Blocks Area.
  3. Each Player chooses two Secondary Colors. They then build a 10-card Personal Codex Deck by selecting from the remaining four Keyword Blocks of their Primary Color and all five Keyword Blocks from their two Secondary Colors (a pool of 14 cards).
  4. Shuffle the Main Deck and deal 5 cards to each Player.

docs.title: 4.1 Turn Phases
docs.text:
1. Ready Phase: Gain EN equal to your Focus (skip on the first turn of the game). Ready all spent units. Remove Player Spent Tokens. EN cannot exceed 10.
  2. Action Phase: Your Player may take two actions. Each of your readied Animations may take one action.
  3. End Phase: Perform the System Refresh (hand size to 5). Check for any Tag triggers.

docs.title: 4.2 Action Menu
docs.text: When an entity takes an action, it becomes spent.

docs.title: 4.2.1-4.2.5 Universal Actions
docs.text:
• Attack: Initiates an Opposed Roll, fueled by discarding cards.
  • Critical Strike: A powerful attack fueled by discarding two cards of the same Power value. The acting unit's Focus is not added to the EV.
  • Support: Remove one damage marker from a friendly unit.
  • Purge: Remove one damage marker from this unit. Optionally, then remove one Status Tag from this unit.
  • Charge: Add 1 EN to your pool.

docs.title: 4.2.6-4.2.7 Player-Only Actions
docs.text:
• Deploy: Pay an Animation's EN cost (equal to its Power) to play it from your hand. You can only take this action if you control fewer Animations than your Focus stat.
  • Equip: Pay an Item's EN cost (its Power) to attach it to a valid unit. Can also be used to move an Item between units.

    • Keywords from Equipped Items

      A unit gains access to the keywords on its equipped Item as Augmented Keywords. The number of these keywords it can use is limited by its own Focus stat. Flaw keywords are always active.

docs.title: 4.3 Opposed Roll Resolution
docs.text:
The following steps resolve in order for an Attack or Critical Strike:

  1. Attacker Action & Fuel: The acting unit becomes spent. The Player discards card(s) from hand.
  2. Calculate Initial Effect Value (EV): EV = Acting Unit's Focus + Power of Discarded Card(s).
    • A Player attacker gains +1 EV for each of their equipped Items.
    • Critical Strike does not add the attacker's Focus to the EV.
  3. Declare Augmented Keyword Use (Attacker): The attacker's controller declares which Augmented Keywords are being used, up to the acting unit's Focus limit. Innate keywords are always active.
  4. Player Keyword Augmentation: A Player performing an Attack or Support may augment it with keywords from their Active Keyword Blocks or equipped Items, up to their Player Focus limit. This is separate from an Animation's keyword use.
  5. Defender Reaction: The defending player may choose one option:
    • Discard one card from hand to add its Power to the RV.
    • Perform a Defensive Sacrifice to add the destroyed Item's Power to the RV.
  6. Calculate Resistance Value (RV): RV = Defender's Focus + Power from defender's chosen option (if any).
  7. Resolution: If EV > RV, the defender receives damage equal to EV - RV. Then, apply all active keyword effects.

Example A: A Player Attacks

The Situation: * Your Player has Focus 2. * Your active Keyword Blocks include Brutal (1.8) and Splash (8.6).

The Action: Your Player performs a Critical Strike.

Resolution: 1. You discard two cards of the same power to fuel the Critical Strike. 2. You calculate the initial EV. 3. Player Keyword Augmentation: Because your Player is performing the action, you can augment it. Your Focus is 2, so you may choose up to two keywords. You choose Brutal and Splash.

Result: The Critical Strike resolves with the effects of both Brutal and Splash applied.

Example B: An Animation Attacks

The Situation: * Your Player has Focus 2 and has the Splash (8.6) keyword active in their Codex. * Your Animation "Hunter" has Focus 1 and an Innate keyword of Martial (1.2). * Hunter is equipped with an Item that grants Piercing (4.6) and Ranged (7.7).

The Action: Your Animation "Hunter" performs an Attack.

Resolution: 1. Innate Keywords: Hunter's Martial keyword is automatically active. 2. Declare Augmented Keyword Use: You check Hunter's equipped Item. Hunter's own Focus is 1, so you may choose only one keyword from its Item. You choose Piercing. 3. Player Keyword Augmentation: This step is skipped. The rule only applies when the Player themself performs the action. You cannot use your Player's Focus to add Splash from your Codex to the Animation's attack.

Result: Hunter's Attack resolves with Martial (innate) and Piercing (from its item) applied.

docs.title: 4.4 Tag Application from Keywords
docs.text:
• Boost Tags (from keywords ending in #.4):
    • On Attack or Critical Strike: Apply to the attacker.
    • On Support: Apply to either the target or the unit performing the action.
  • Status Tags (from keywords ending in #.5):
    • Typically applied to the target of the effect or action.

docs.title: 5.1 Gaining Karma (Gain 1)
docs.text:
• When one of your Attack or Critical Strike actions successfully deals 1 or more damage.
  • When you perform a Critical Strike.
  • When you destroy an enemy Animation or the enemy Player.

docs.title: 5.2 Spending Karma
docs.text:
Spending Karma does not use a Player action but can only be done during your Action Phase.

  • Cost 1 Karma (System Tweak)
    • Overclock: Draw one card.
    • Re-engage: Ready one unit or remove its Suppressed state.
  • Cost 3 Karma (The Tactical Path)
    • Acquire Codex: Draw one card from your Personal Codex Deck and activate it.
  • The Strategic Path: Refine Focus
    • Effect: Permanently increase your Player's Focus stat by 1.
    • Cost: The Karma cost is equal to your current Focus stat + 1.
      • Focus 1 -> 2 costs 2 Karma.
      • Focus 2 -> 3 costs 3 Karma.
      • Focus 3 -> 4 costs 4 Karma, etc.

docs.title: Animation Card
docs.text:
1. Power (PWR): A value of 1-5 in the top left corner. Represents EN Cost, HP, and discard value.
  2. Focus (FCS): A value of 1-5 in the center. Represents combat skill and capacity for Augmented Keywords.
  3. Keywords: A maximum of 3 keywords in the text box.

docs.title: Item Card
docs.text:
1. Power (PWR) & EN Cost: A single value (1-3) in the top left corner that serves as both EN Cost to play and Power for discards or Defensive Sacrifice.
  2. Keywords: A maximum of 3 total keywords. The number of non-Flaw keywords cannot exceed the Item's EN Cost.

docs.title: Codex Card
docs.text: A reference card listing the two keywords from its block with their descriptions.

docs.title: Player Card
docs.text: A visual representation of the Player, performing no direct game function.

docs.title: Appendix C: Keyword List
docs.text:
Note

Not all keywords in this list may appear on cards in the base Faction Modules; some may only appear on Codex Cards or in future content.

Color 0: Null

  • 0.0 Restricted: Your Player's Deploy and Equip actions cost +1 EN.
  • 0.1 Aura: Your Player's attack gains +1 EV.
  • 0.2 Specialist: After Your Player attacks with this keyword, you may draw one card.
  • 0.3 Alert: After Your Player attacks with this keyword, pay 1 EN to return one of Your Items to Your hand.
  • 0.4 Liberate: Apply the Liberate Tag.
  • 0.5 Mark: Apply the Mark Tag.
  • 0.6 Indirect: When defending against this attack, the defender reveals the top card of the Main Deck and adds its Power to the RV instead of discarding from hand.
  • 0.7 Adaptive: When Your Player's attack deals damage, you may have the target's controller discard a card instead of placing damage markers.
  • 0.8 Gamble: When Your Player performs an Attack action augmented with this keyword, after declaring the initial card(s) discarded from hand to fuel the attack: You may choose to reveal cards one at a time from the top of the Main Deck. For each card revealed this way: place one damage marker on Your Player, this attack gains +1 EV, and the revealed card is placed into the Discard Pile. You may stop revealing cards at any time. This occurs before the Defender Reaction step.
  • 0.9 Edit: If this unit's attack is successful, you may pay 1 EN to add any keyword that shares a color with the target’s faction.

Color 1: Silver

  • 1.0 Bane: Choose a Color. When this unit is attacked, reduce its RV by 1 for each keyword of the chosen Color used in the attack.
  • 1.1 Traveller: Your Player's action can target a Player even if they control Animations.
  • 1.2 Martial: After an Opposed Roll targeting this unit is fully resolved, if this unit was not destroyed, it deals 1 damage to the attacking unit. This damage is not an attack and cannot be prevented or reduced.
  • 1.3 Attuned: Your Player's attack uses a chosen friendly Animation's Focus for its EV calculation instead of Your Player's.
  • 1.4 Augment: Apply the Augment Tag.
  • 1.5 Impair: Apply the Impair Tag.
  • 1.6 Reactive: As a reaction when one of Your units is targeted by an attack, you may discard a card from Your hand to add its Power to the defending unit's RV. This does not replace the normal discard option.
  • 1.7 Phasing: Your Player's attack's damage cannot be reduced or prevented by keyword effects.
  • 1.8 Brutal: A Critical Strike with this keyword deals 1 additional damage.
  • 1.9 Translocate: When this keyword is used in an Attack action: Instead of performing an Opposed Roll, you may choose to return the target Animation or Item to its owner's hand. If you do, the attack sequence ends.

Color 2: Yellow

  • 2.0 Anxious: This unit cannot perform Critical Strike.
  • 2.1 Acrobatic: After this unit attacks, it cannot be targeted by attacks until the start of Your next turn.
  • 2.2 Sentry: When Your Player attacks with this keyword, you may look at the defending Player's hand.
  • 2.3 Eidetic: The first time Your Player attacks an enemy unit with this keyword, the attack gains +1 EV.
  • 2.4 Haste: Apply the Haste Tag.
  • 2.5 Slow: Apply the Slow Tag.
  • 2.6 Snap: Resolve Your Player's attack as Attacker's Focus vs. Defender's Focus. No cards are discarded for Power.
  • 2.7 Two-Handed: If this unit has an Item equipped, its attacks gain +1 EV.
  • 2.8 Rapid: When Your Player performs an Attack action with this keyword: After this attack resolves, you may spend 1 EN. If you do, this attack immediately triggers again against the same target. This entire sequence counts as a single Attack action.
  • 2.9 Reckless: When this unit attacks, its controller discards one card from hand and reveals the top card of the Main Deck. They choose one to set the attack's power. EV = Power of chosen card. RV = 0. (Focus is not used, and the defender cannot discard.) After resolution, place both cards into the Discard Pile.

Color 3: Green

  • 3.0 Hesitant: When this unit is defending, its controller cannot discard a card to add to its RV.
  • 3.1 Sturdy: This unit is unaffected by effects that would reduce its Focus.
  • 3.2 Brawler: When Your Player attacks with this keyword and deals damage, look at the defender's hand and choose a card for them to discard.
  • 3.3 Stubborn: When one of Your Animations is destroyed, you may draw one card.
  • 3.4 Ward: Apply the Ward Tag.
  • 3.5 Daze: Apply the Daze Tag.
  • 3.6 Sculpt: Your Player's attack gains +X EV, where X is the number of Animations you control.
  • 3.7 Defensive: When this unit is defending, its controller may discard one additional card from their hand to add its Power to the RV.
  • 3.8 Impact: If Your Player's attack deals damage, the target becomes "spent" and does not ready during its controller's next Ready Phase.
  • 3.9 Shift: When this unit makes a support action, you may move any number of Items equipped to Your units to any other valid targets you control.

Color 4: Black

  • 4.0 Feeble: This unit has -1 Focus.
  • 4.1 Survivor: If this unit would be destroyed by damage, its controller may discard one card from their hand. If they do, prevent that damage and the unit becomes Suppressed.
  • 4.2 Stoic: An Attack with this keyword cannot be a Critical Strike. For each card that would be discarded for EV, you may choose not to. If you do, the attack's EV is calculated as Attacker's Focus + Attacker's Focus.
  • 4.3 Ageless: Your units are unaffected by the Blight Tag and the effects of the Growth keyword.
  • 4.4 Bless: Apply the Bless Tag.
  • 4.5 Curse: Apply the Curse Tag.
  • 4.6 Piercing: Your Player's attack deals damage to its target and the enemy Player simultaneously.
  • 4.7 Flux: Your Player may place damage markers on themself to give their attack +X EV, where X is the number of markers placed.
  • 4.8 Siphon: If Your Player's attack deals damage, remove 1 damage marker from Your Player.
  • 4.9 Animate: As part of an Attack action with this keyword, you may target an Animation card in the discard pile and put it into Your hand.

Color 5: Orange

  • 5.0 Gremlins: If this unit is dealt damage from an attack and its controller did not discard a card to add to the RV, destroy one Item equipped to this unit.
  • 5.1 Sensor: When you Deploy an Animation, look at the top card of the Main Deck. You may put it on the bottom.
  • 5.2 Improvisor: As part of an action, choose one keyword effect from any Item you control. This action gains that keyword for its resolution.
  • 5.3 Crafty: Your Equip action costs 1 less EN (min 1).
  • 5.4 Charge: Apply the Charge Tag.
  • 5.5 Bind: Apply the Bind Tag.
  • 5.6 Imbue: As part of an action, choose one additional keyword from any of Your Player's active Keyword Blocks. This action gains that keyword for its resolution.
  • 5.7 Material: When using this keyword for an Attack, you may destroy one of Your equipped Items. If you do, the defender cannot discard a card for their RV.
  • 5.8 Leverage: Your Player's attack gains +X EV, where X is the number of Items you control.
  • 5.9 Manifest: As part of an Attack action with this keyword, reveal the top card of the Main Deck. If it is an Item, put it into Your hand. Otherwise, discard it.

Color 6: White

  • 6.0 Vulnerable: Critical Strike actions targeting this unit deal 1 additional damage.
  • 6.1 Tolerant: For each unit with this keyword: while its number of Status Tags is less than or equal to its Focus, those Tags are inactive for that unit.
  • 6.2 Deadeye: Your Player may target an Item on the defending unit. If the attack deals damage, destroy that Item instead of placing damage markers.
  • 6.3 Immunized: Choose a Status Tag when you acquire this block. For the remainder of the game, Your units cannot be affected by that Tag.
  • 6.4 Cure: Apply the Cure Tag.
  • 6.5 Weaken: Apply the Weaken Tag.
  • 6.6 Sticky: If Your Player's attack deals damage, the target becomes Suppressed.
  • 6.7 Restore: When this unit performs a Support action, the target removes 1 additional damage marker.
  • 6.8 Exploit: Your Player's attack gains +1 EV for each Status Tag on its target.
  • 6.9 Growth: While a unit with Growth is spent, all other friendly Animations gain +1 Focus.

Color 7: Red

  • 7.0 Limited: This unit's maximum HP is reduced by 1.
  • 7.1 Resilient: Your Player's maximum HP is increased by 1.
  • 7.2 Font: If you have gained at least 1 Karma this turn, Your Player's attacks gain +1 EV.
  • 7.3 Insulated: when this unit is attacked the attacking unit cannot use augmented keywords.
  • 7.4 Regen: Apply the Regen Tag.
  • 7.5 Blight: Apply the Blight Tag.
  • 7.6 Area: An attack with this keyword does not have an Opposed Roll. Instead, it deals 1 damage to each enemy Animation. The defending player may pay 1 EN per Animation to prevent the damage to it.
  • 7.7 Ranged: When used in an Attack or Critical Strike, neither the attacker's nor defender's Focus is added to the EV/RV calculation.
  • 7.8 Multiply: When used in an Attack, choose two different enemy units. Conduct two separate Opposed Roll Resolutions against each target, using the same full EV for both.
  • 7.9 Split: Instead of the normal Support effect, destroy one friendly Animation. Deploy a number of Power 1 / Focus 1 'Echo' tokens equal to the destroyed Animation's Power. Echoes enter readied and do not count toward Your Command Limit.

Color 8: Blue

  • 8.0 Awkward: When this unit attacks, its controller must discard one additional card from hand for no effect.
  • 8.1 Charismatic: When you Deploy an Animation, you may force an opponent to discard a card.
  • 8.2 Leader: When Your Player attacks with this keyword, all of Your Animations gain +1 Power until Your next turn.
  • 8.3 Insightful: whenever this unit makes a Support action, its controller may draw a card.
  • 8.4 Enhance: Apply the Enhance Tag.
  • 8.5 Silence: Apply the Silence Tag.
  • 8.6 Splash: If Your Player's attack deals damage, apply its keyword effects (but not damage) to one other enemy Animation.
  • 8.7 Lingering: If Your Player's attack applies a Status Tag, it cannot be removed until the end of the target's controller's next turn.
  • 8.8 Spread: If Your Player's attack deals damage, choose another enemy Animation. That Animation takes 1 damage.
  • 8.9 Potent: When resolving Your Player's attack, you may choose for it to deal no damage. If you do, its keyword effects apply even if the EV did not exceed the RV.

Color 9: Purple

  • 9.0 Mundane: Your Player cannot augment this unit's attacks with their personal keywords.
  • 9.1 Aware: When an opponent plays an Item, you may pay 1 EN to draw one card.
  • 9.2 Stealthy: When an opponent targets a unit with this keyword, they must pay 1 additional EN as a cost.
  • 9.3 Trickster: As a reaction when an opponent declares an Attack, you may discard a card. If you do, the attacking player must also discard a card for no effect.
  • 9.4 Obscure: Apply the Obscure Tag.
  • 9.5 Nullify: Apply the Nullify Tag.
  • 9.6 Chain: If this unit's Attack or Critical Strike destroys its target, you may immediately place 1 damage marker on another enemy unit.
  • 9.7 Natural: Your Player may have one additional Item equipped beyond their Focus limit.
  • 9.8 Ambience: When this unit attacks, its controller may choose not to discard a card. If they do, search the discard pile for the card with the highest Power and add that value to this attack's EV.
  • 9.9 Channel: When a unit ('the Channeler') uses this keyword, choose another friendly unit ('the Source'). The Channeler becomes spent. The action resolves as if performed by the Source, using the Source's stats and keywords, but the Channeler's controller makes all decisions.

docs.title: Tag Classifications
docs.text:
• Boost Tags: Applied by keywords ending in #.4.
  • Status Tags: Applied by keywords ending in #.5.

docs.title: Defined Boost Tags
docs.text: Liberate (0.4), Augment (1.4), Haste (2.4), Ward (3.4), Bless (4.4), Charge (5.4), Cure (6.4), Regen (7.4), Enhance (8.4), Obscure (9.4).

docs.title: Defined Status Tags
docs.text: Mark (0.5), Impair (1.5), Slow (2.5), Daze (3.5), Curse (4.5), Bind (5.5), Weaken (6.5), Blight (7.5), Silence (8.5), Nullify (9.5).

docs.title: Individual Tag Definitions
docs.text:
1. Liberate Tag: Remove this Tag from a Suppressed unit to ready it (not an action).
  2. Mark Tag: Attacks targeting this unit gain +1 EV.
  3. Augment Tag: Remove this Tag when the unit attacks to gain a keyword effect from one of its controller’s active Codex Cards for the attack.
  4. Impair Tag: This unit has -1 Focus (min 0).
  5. Haste Tag: Remove this Tag from a spent unit to ready it (not an action).
  6. Slow Tag: This unit does not ready during the Ready Phase. Its controller may spend 1 EN during the Ready Phase to remove this Tag.
  7. Ward Tag: The first time this unit would be dealt damage, prevent that damage and remove this Tag.
  8. Daze Tag: This unit cannot contribute Power from discarded cards when attacking or defending.
  9. Bless Tag: When this unit would be dealt damage, remove this Tag to prevent 1 of that damage.
  10. Curse Tag: Damage markers cannot be removed from this unit.
  11. Charge Tag: When an Animation with this Tag takes the Charge action, gain an additional 1 EN, then remove this Tag.
  12. Bind Tag: This unit cannot perform Attack or Critical Strike actions.
  13. Cure Tag: On gain, remove one Status Tag from this unit, then remove this Tag. If it has no Status Tags, this Tag remains and prevents the next one that would be applied.
  14. Weaken Tag: This unit's Attack or Critical Strike actions have -1 EV.
  15. Regen Tag: At the start of its controller's Ready Phase, this unit removes 1 damage marker from itself.
  16. Blight Tag: Whenever this unit performs any action, place 1 damage marker on it after the action resolves.
  17. Enhance Tag: In an Opposed Roll, this unit's controller may discard an additional card to add its Power to the EV or RV.
  18. Silence Tag: This unit's printed keywords are inactive.
  19. Obscure Tag: When an opponent attacks this unit, they must discard two cards and use the lower Power value for the EV.
  20. Nullify Tag: On gain, remove one Boost Tag from this unit, then remove this Tag. If it has no Boost Tags, this Tag remains and prevents the next one that would be applied.

docs.title: I. Game Start & Setup
docs.text:
1. Determine Starting Player (highest d10 roll).
  2. Perform World Weaving, Player Mat setup, Codex selection, and deal hands.

docs.title: II. Your Turn Structure
docs.text:
A. Ready Phase 1. Gain EN: Gain EN equal to your Player's Focus (skip on game's first turn). 2. Ready Units: Turn all spent Animations upright. 3. Remove Tokens: Remove all Player Spent Tokens from your Mat.

B. Action Phase * Player Actions: Take up to two (2) actions. * Animation Actions: Each readied Animation may take one (1) action. * Spend Karma: Use Karma abilities at any time during this phase (not an action). * End Turn: You may end your turn at any time (not mid-action).

C. End Phase 1. System Refresh: Adjust hand size to exactly 5 (draw or discard). 2. Tag Triggers: Resolve any end-of-turn Tag effects.

docs.title: III. Opposed Roll Resolution (Attack / Critical Strike)
docs.text:
1. Attacker Action & Fuel: Attacker becomes spent. Discard card(s).
  2. Calculate Initial EV.
  3. Declare Augmented Keywords (if an Animation is attacking).
  4. Player Keyword Augmentation (if the Player is attacking).
  5. Defender Reaction: Defender chooses to discard a card, perform a Defensive Sacrifice, or do nothing.
  6. Calculate RV.
  7. Resolution: Compare EV to RV, deal damage if EV > RV, and apply all keyword effects.

docs.title: Game Objective
docs.text: Be the first to reduce your opponent's HP from 10 to 0.

docs.title: Your Player Mat
docs.text:
• HP: Starts at 10.
  • EN: Starts at 10. Resource for playing cards.
  • Focus: Starts at 1. Your skill, command limit, and item limit.
  • Karma: Starts at 0. Special resource for powerful effects.

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text:
• Units: Your Player and your Animations.
  • Animations: Your creatures. Their Power (P) is their HP, EN cost, and discard value. Their Focus (F) limits their use of Item keywords.
  • Items: Equipment that grants keywords.
  • Guardian Precedence: You must defeat a Player's Animations before you can attack them directly.

docs.title: Your Turn Simplified
docs.text:
1. Ready Phase: Gain EN equal to your Focus, ready all your units.
  2. Action Phase: Your Player takes 2 actions; each Animation takes 1.
  3. End Phase: Adjust your hand to 5 cards.

docs.title: Core Actions
docs.text:
• Deploy (Player-Only): Pay an Animation's Power in EN to play it. It enters spent. You can't have more Animations than your Focus stat.
  • Attack (Universal):
    1. Declare attacker and target.
    2. Discard a card to fuel the attack.
    3. Calculate EV (Focus + Power of Card).
    4. Defender reacts (discards a card or sacrifices an item).
    5. Calculate RV (Focus + Power of Defender's Card/Item).
    6. If EV > RV, deal damage equal to the difference.

docs.title: Spending Karma
docs.text:
• 1 Karma: Draw a card (Overclock) or ready a unit (Re-engage).
  • 3 Karma: Get a new Keyword Block from your Codex (Acquire Codex).
  • Current Focus + 1 Karma: Permanently increase your Focus (Refine Focus). This is a key long-term strategy!

docs.title: 1.0 OBJECTIVE
docs.text: The last player with Health Points (HP) remaining is the winner. The game is played until all other players have had their HP reduced from 10 to 0.

docs.title: 2.0 GAME FORMATS
docs.text:
• Duel: A two-player, head-to-head match.
  • Arena: A 3-4 player free-for-all.

docs.title: 3.0 COMPONENTS
docs.text:
• 1x Agent Board per player.
  • 10x ten-sided dice (d10s): One for each of the 10 system Colors (0-9).
  • Keyword Tokens: For digital play, the token pool is considered infinite.
  • Tag Tokens: For the 10 Boost and 10 Status tags.

docs.title: 4.0 SETUP
docs.text:
1. Each player takes an Agent Board.
  2. Set starting values: HP = 10, Focus = 1, Karma = 0.
  3. Archetype Declaration: Each player chooses a Primary Color and two Secondary Colors to form their 3-Color Archetype.
  4. Determine the first player. Play proceeds clockwise.

docs.title: 5.0 CORE CONCEPTS
docs.text:
• 5.1 Affinity Matrix: A 3x3 grid for your Keyword Tokens. Each slot has a maximum capacity of 5 tokens. If generating a new Keyword Token would cause a slot to exceed this limit, you must choose and discard one of the existing tokens from that slot to make room for the new one.
  • 5.2 Focus: Determines the complexity of your actions; it's the maximum number of Keyword Tokens you can spend on a single Keyword Activation. The maximum Focus is 5.
  • 5.3 Karma: The primary resource for generating tokens. The maximum Karma is 10.
  • 5.4 Successful Activation:
    • An activation targeting an opponent is "successful" if it is not Avoided and directly causes one or more of the following:
      • The target loses at least 1 HP from the activation's final calculated damage.
      • A Status Tag is successfully applied to the target.
      • A Keyword Token the target controls is discarded, swapped, altered, or removed.
      • The target loses Karma as a direct result of the activation's effect.
    • An activation targeting yourself is automatically successful.
    • Losing resources to pay the cost of a Respond action does not count as a successful outcome for the attacker.

Damage vs. Life Loss

  • Damage: The reduction of HP that occurs from an activation's resolution. Effects that trigger "when you take damage" only apply to this. Damage can often be Resisted.
  • Life Loss: The reduction of HP from paying costs or from non-activation effects. This is not considered "damage" and cannot be Resisted.

docs.title: 6.0 THE CORE LOOP: TURN STRUCTURE
docs.text:
A player's turn is a cycle of four phases following a strict sequence of Declaration -> Response -> Resolution.

  1. Ready (Upkeep Phase): Resolve "start of turn" effects. Your Ready phase then proceeds in this strict order:
    • Gain Resources: Gain Karma equal to your current Focus.
    • Free Generation: Perform one free Keyword Token generation. You must choose your Primary Color for this; roll a d10 to determine the token's category (the result of the die).
    • Paid Generation: You may now spend Karma to generate additional Keyword Tokens by rolling a d10. The costs are:
      • 1 Karma: Choose one of your three Affinity Colors or the Null [0] Color.
      • 2 Karma: Choose any non-Affinity Color.
  2. Activate (Action Phase): Perform one primary action from the list in section 7.0.
  3. Respond (Reaction Phase): Targeted player(s) independently choose to Resist, Avoid, or Do Not React.
  4. Resolve & Reward (Resolution Phase): Effects are finalized. If your activation was successful against an opponent, you gain 1 Karma (plus any combo bonuses). If multiple effects trigger simultaneously, you (the active player) choose the order of resolution.

docs.title: 7.1 Activate Actions
docs.text:
• Basic Activation: Spend no tokens. Deals 1 damage. This can be enhanced with a Karma Surge by spending 2 Karma for +1 damage.
  • Keyword Activation: Spend Keyword Tokens up to your Focus value to add their effects to the activation.
  • Self-Targeted Activation: An activation that targets yourself. It is automatically successful, deals no damage, and grants no Karma reward.
  • Focus Break: Spend 5 of your Affinity Color tokens to permanently increase your Focus by 1.
  • Resonance Lock-In: Spend 2-3 identical tokens to gain that Keyword's permanent Passive Effect. (Note: .2 Talent keywords cost 2 tokens; all others cost 3).

docs.title: 7.2 Respond Actions (Reactions)
docs.text:
• Resist: Spend any Keyword Token to prevent 1 damage. You may also spend 2 Karma to prevent 1 damage.
  • Avoid: To Avoid, you must spend Keyword Tokens from your Matrix to exactly match the color of each token the active player spent for their activation. If the cost is paid, the entire instance of the activation is negated.
    • Your Focus does not limit the number of tokens you can spend to pay an Avoid cost.
    • "Spent" tokens are those that count toward the attacker's Focus limit. Tokens included via a .0 Flaw or .3 Quirk effect are not considered 'spent' and do not need to be matched.

docs.title: 8.1 Combos & Special Activations
docs.text:
These are specific Keyword Activations that can be performed even if their token cost exceeds your Focus.

Chroma Burst

  • Requirement: Spend 3 or more tokens of the same color.

  • Effect: All of their effects resolve simultaneously.

  • Bonus: +1 Karma

    If this activation is successful, you gain 1 bonus Karma in addition to the standard reward.

Resonance Cascade

  • Requirement: Spend exactly 3 tokens (one from each of your three Affinity Colors).

  • Effect: Their effects resolve as normal. This is primarily a play for resources.

  • Bonus: +2 Karma

    If this activation is successful, you gain a large bonus of 2 Karma.

Critical Activation

  • Requirement: Spend 5 tokens of the same color.

  • Effect Replacement

    This activation does not use the keywords' normal Active Effects. Instead, its entire effect becomes the following:

    "Deal damage to the target's HP equal to your current Focus. The target also loses Karma equal to your current Focus."

  • Bonus: +3 Karma

    If this activation is successful, you gain a massive bonus of 3 Karma.

docs.title: 8.2 Tags (Boosts & Statuses)
docs.text:
• Boosts (self-targeted via .4 keywords) are always successfully applied.
  • Statuses (opponent-targeted via .5 keywords) are conditional on a successful activation.
  • Multiple instances of the same tag on a player stack and resolve independently.

docs.title: 8.3 Entity Rules
docs.text:
An entity is a temporary body on the board created by a keyword's effect.

  • They are considered "players" and are legal targets for any activation.
  • They are removed from play when their HP is reduced to 0.
  • Default Rule on Defeat: Unless an effect states otherwise (e.g., the [7.9] Split passive), when an entity is removed from play, any unspent Keyword Tokens on its micro-Matrix are discarded.

docs.title: Manifested Guardian (The Shield)
docs.text:
• Created By: [5.9] Manifest
  • Creation Rules: When created, set the Guardian's starting HP equal to your current Focus.
  • Function: While the Guardian is active, opponents must target it instead of your Agent, unless an effect specifically allows it to be ignored (e.g., [7.7] Ranged).

docs.title: Split Entity (The Partner)
docs.text:
• Created By: [7.9] Split
  • Creation Rules: When created, you sacrifice an amount of your HP and temporarily reduce your Focus. These amounts become the entity's starting HP and Focus. The other tokens spent on the activation form its starting micro-Matrix.
  • Function: During your Activate phase, you may perform one action with your Agent and one with your Split Entity, in the order of your choice.

docs.title: Token Entity (The Summon)
docs.text:
• Created By: [4.9] Animate
  • Creation Rules: When created, set the entity's starting HP and Focus equal to your current Focus. The other tokens spent form its starting micro-Matrix.
  • Function: You temporarily set your Agent board aside and act as the Token Entity, using its HP, Focus, and micro-Matrix. Your Agent cannot be targeted or affected while you are the entity.

docs.title: 9.0 GLOBAL RULES & HIERARCHY
docs.text:
• 9.1 Keyword Application:
    • An activation cannot include more than one instance of the same named keyword.
    • A .0 Flaw cannot "carry" another .0 Flaw.

  • 9.2 Effect Hierarchy:

    The Golden Rule: 'Cannot' Trumps 'Can'

    If one game effect states that something can happen, and another effect states that it cannot, the effect that prohibits the action always takes precedence.

    • Copying is Not Stealing: Effects that "copy" a token or passive do not affect the original owner.
    • Unstoppable vs. Immunity: Effects that "cannot be Resisted or Avoided" refer only to Respond actions and do not bypass permanent passive immunities.

docs.title: 10.0 KEYWORD CATEGORY TRAITS
docs.text:
• .0 Flaw: Suffer a drawback to use another token's effect without spending it.
  • .1 Gift: Utility effects. Can be spent during the Ready phase for 1 Karma instead of their normal effect.
  • .2 Talent: Permanent upgrades. A Resonance Lock-In for a Talent costs 2 identical tokens (instead of the usual 3).
  • .3 Quirk: Free "rider" effects that can be added to an activation without costing Focus (limit 1 Quirk per activation).
  • .4 Boost: Applies a beneficial, guaranteed Boost Tag to yourself.
  • .5 Status: Applies a detrimental Status Tag to an opponent, but only on a successful activation.
  • .6 Form: Alters how an activation targets opponents.
  • .7 Modifier: Bends the core rules of an action or the game state.
  • .8 Drive: Directly increases numerical efficiency and interacts with damage.
  • .9 Unique: Game-altering "ultimate" abilities.

docs.title: 11.0 COMPLETE KEYWORD CODEX (v10.4)
docs.text:
Null [0]Silver [1]Yellow [2]Green [3]Black [4]Orange [5]White [6]Red [7]Blue [8]Purple [9]
  • [0.0] Restricted (.Flaw):
    • Active: Choose a "carried" Keyword Token from one of your three Affinity Color slots; its Active Effect is applied, but the token is not spent.
    • Passive: Your max Karma is reduced to 5. Your free Keyword Token roll during the Ready phase is modified: you may choose to roll for any of your three Affinity Colors, instead of being restricted to only your Primary Color.
  • [0.1] Aura (.Gift):
    • Active: This activation deals +1 damage for each other Keyword Token spent from your Primary Affinity Color.
    • Passive: Any activation you perform that includes at least one Keyword Token of your Primary Affinity Color deals +1 damage.
  • [0.2] Specialist (.Talent):
    • Active: Deals +1 damage for each Keyword Token spent that shares a category with another token in this activation.
    • Passive: The first activation each turn that includes 2+ Keyword Tokens from the same category deals +1 damage.
  • [0.3] Alert (.Quirk):
    • Active: The target must pay 1 Karma as a cost to perform a Resist or Avoid action.
    • Passive: The first Keyword Token you spend during your Respond phase each turn is returned to your Matrix.
  • [0.4] Liberate (.Boost):
    • Active: Apply the Liberate Boost Tag.
    • Passive: Any Boost you apply can be a Liberate tag instead.
    • Liberate Tag: Expend to prevent a Keyword Token from being discarded by an opponent's effect.
  • [0.5] Mark (.Status):
    • Active: If successful, apply the Mark Status Tag.
    • Passive: Any Status you apply can be a Mark tag instead.
    • Mark Tag: The next time this player takes damage from any source, they take +1 damage. Remove this tag.
  • [0.6] Indirect (.Form):
    • Active: The target cannot Resist or Avoid unless they first discard a Keyword Token that matches your Primary Color.
    • Passive: You take 1 less damage from activations with a .6 Form keyword.
  • [0.7] Adaptive (.Modifier):
    • Active: During resolution, you may have this activation's damage become either: Target loses 2 Karma, or Target discards one Keyword Token.
    • Passive: Once per turn, you may spend a Keyword Token of any color as if it were one of your Affinity Colors.
  • [0.8] Gamble (.Drive):
    • Active: Roll two d10s (Color, Category). This activation gains the Active Effect of the resulting keyword.
    • Passive: Once per turn, you may reroll any single d10 you have rolled. You must accept the new result.
  • [0.9] Edit (.Unique):
    • Active: Swap a number of Keyword Tokens on your Matrix with an equal number on the target's Matrix, up to your Focus. This cannot be Resisted or Avoided.
    • Passive: Once per turn, when rolling the d10 for your Primary Color, you may choose the result instead.
  • [1.0] Bane (.Flaw):
    • Active: You suffer 1 Life Loss. Carry another token.
    • Passive: Your activations deal +1 damage to targets with higher HP than you.
  • [1.1] Traveller (.Gift):
    • Active: Choose another token in this activation; it is considered one of your Affinity Colors for combo requirements.
    • Passive: Your first non-Affinity die roll each turn costs 1 Karma instead of 2.
  • [1.2] Martial (.Talent):
    • Active: If the target's Resist reduces damage to 0, the activation is unsuccessful, but the target suffers 1 Life Loss anyway.
    • Passive: Your Karma Surges cost 1 Karma for +1 damage.
  • [1.3] Attuned (.Quirk):
    • Active: If successful and includes a Primary Color token, gain 1 bonus Karma.
    • Passive: Once per turn, when an opponent activates a keyword matching one of your Affinity Colors, you may gain 1 Karma.
  • [1.4] Augment (.Boost):
    • Active: Apply the Augment Boost Tag.
    • Passive: Any Boost you apply can be an Augment tag instead.
    • Augment Tag: Expend when rolling a d10 for generation to roll two dice and choose one result.
  • [1.5] Impair (.Status):
    • Active: If successful, apply the Impair Status Tag.
    • Passive: Any Status you apply can be an Impair tag instead.
    • Impair Tag: The next time this player spends Karma, the cost is increased by 1. Remove this tag.
  • [1.6] Reactive (.Form):
    • Active: If this activation is Avoided or fully Resisted, you may return one of the other spent tokens to your Matrix.
    • Passive: When you successfully Avoid or fully Resist an activation, you gain 1 Karma.
  • [1.7] Phasing (.Modifier):
    • Active: The target cannot perform a Resist action. They may still Avoid.
    • Passive: Opponents must spend one additional Keyword Token as part of the cost of any Resist action against you.
  • [1.8] Brutal (.Drive):
    • Active: Deals +1 damage. The target cannot gain Karma or tokens from keyword effects during this activation's resolution.
    • Passive: When you deal 3+ damage with a single activation, the target loses 1 Karma.
  • [1.9] Translocate (.Unique):
    • Active: Swap one of your other spent tokens with a token on the target's Matrix; the stolen token's effect is added to this activation.
    • Passive: At the end of your turn, you may swap one token on your Matrix with a token on an opponent's Matrix.
  • [2.0] Anxious (.Flaw):
    • Active: Discard a token from your Matrix. Roll a d10; this activation gains the effect of the keyword of the discarded token's Color and the rolled Category.
    • Passive: During your Ready phase, you may discard a token to reroll its category.
  • [2.1] Acrobatic (.Gift):
    • Active: If this activation is Avoided, choose a token on your Matrix. The target must discard a token sharing its Color or Category, or the Avoid fails.
    • Passive: The first time your activation is Avoided each turn, you may reroll the category of one token on your Matrix.
  • [2.2] Sentry (.Talent):
    • Active: If this activation is Avoided, the target suffers 1 Life Loss. This does not make the activation successful.
    • Passive: When you successfully Avoid or fully Resist an activation, the active player suffers 1 Life Loss.
  • [2.3] Eidetic (.Quirk):
    • Active: If successful, generate a copy of a token on the target's Matrix.
    • Passive: Once per turn, when generating a token, you may pay 1 extra Karma to generate a second, identical token.
  • [2.4] Haste (.Boost):
    • Active: Apply the Haste Boost Tag.
    • Passive: Any Boost you apply can be a Haste tag instead.
    • Haste Tag: Expend at the start of your Ready phase to perform a second, additional Ready phase this turn.
  • [2.5] Slow (.Status):
    • Active: If successful, apply the Slow Status Tag.
    • Passive: Any Status you apply can be a Slow tag instead.
    • Slow Tag: During your next Ready phase, your Focus is treated as 1 lower. Remove this tag at the end of that phase.
  • [2.6] Snap (.Form):
    • Active: The target cannot perform any Respond actions. This activation's damage is 1 and can only include one .5 Status.
    • Passive: You are immune to the active effect of Snap. When targeted by an activation that includes Snap, you may perform Respond actions normally.
  • [2.7] Condense (.Modifier):
    • Active: Deals bonus damage equal to (your Focus - tokens spent).
    • Passive: Focus Break costs 4 Affinity tokens instead of 5.
  • [2.8] Rapid (.Drive):
    • Active: This activation's damage is dealt as a sequence of 1-damage instances. Only the first successful instance can apply tags. (Note: Each instance of 1 damage in the sequence can be Resisted independently.)
    • Passive: Damage from your Basic Activations and Karma Surges is dealt as a sequence of 1-damage instances.
  • [2.9] Reckless (.Unique):
    • Active: You may suffer any amount of Life Loss; this activation deals +1 damage for each HP lost this way.
